item.title: NFL Playoff Picture Week 7: All 4 NFC North teams are in the field for now
item.description: Entering Week 7, we're about only one-third of the way through the regular season. So what good is a playoff lookahead this early, especially one where last season's champs (Seahawks) and this season's favorites (Rams) are not included? You might be surprised. On the one hand, if we look at the Week 6 standings from the 2025 season , you'd notice that the Colts and Buccaneers were the top two seeds in each respective conference. Neither team ended up making the playoffs. On the other hand, the fields were not that out of whack from what we eventually saw in the playoffs. Six of the seven AFC teams and five of the seven NFC teams that were in the playoff field after Week 6 eventually made the postseason. So there are certainly some big-picture things we can take from the current playoff field. It gives some perspective on just how much ground preseason playoff favorites, such as the Rams and Texans, have to make up if they want in on the playoff party come January. Here's the current playoff field if the regular season ended today. (Yahoo Sports) It also shows just how strong the NFC North is now, with all four teams currently projected to make the postseason. Since the playoff format expanded in 2020, no division has ever landed all four teams in a single playoff field. Here is the current playoff field entering Week 7, listed by divisional seed: AFC 1. Chiefs The unbeaten Chiefs own the best point differential (plus-57) in the NFL, and three of their five victories have been quite comfortable. Kenneth Walker III (655 rushing yards, the most ever by a player in his first five games with a team) has been a godsend, Patrick Mahomes has looked mostly terrific coming off injury, and KC's defense is allowing the second-fewest points per game. But they haven't faced a battering ram of a schedule so far, and six of their next eight games are on the road, so we are going to find out just how real they are over the next two months. 2. Bills Buffalo hits the bye week in great shape at 5-1, but there have been some close-shave victories (and a home loss to the Patriots) among them. Josh Allen has been mostly tremendous in leading the NFL's top-scoring offense, but he's also had to do most of the heavy lifting at times. The run defense has shown improvement from a year ago, but virtually every other aspect of the defense as a whole could use improvement. item.content:encoded: Entering Week 7, we're about only one-third of the way through the regular season. So what good is a playoff lookahead this early, especially one where last season's champs (Seahawks) and this season's favorites (Rams) are not included? You might be surprised. On the one hand, if we look at the Week 6 standings from the 2025 season , you'd notice that the Colts and Buccaneers were the top two seeds in each respective conference. Neither team ended up making the playoffs. On the other hand, the fields were not that out of whack from what we eventually saw in the playoffs. Six of the seven AFC teams and five of the seven NFC teams that were in the playoff field after Week 6 eventually made the postseason. So there are certainly some big-picture things we can take from the current playoff field. It gives some perspective on just how much ground preseason playoff favorites, such as the Rams and Texans, have to make up if they want in on the playoff party come January. Here's the current playoff field if the regular season ended today. (Yahoo Sports) It also shows just how strong the NFC North is now, with all four teams currently projected to make the postseason. Since the playoff format expanded in 2020, no division has ever landed all four teams in a single playoff field. Here is the current playoff field entering Week 7, listed by divisional seed: AFC 1. Chiefs The unbeaten Chiefs own the best point differential (plus-57) in the NFL, and three of their five victories have been quite comfortable. Kenneth Walker III (655 rushing yards, the most ever by a player in his first five games with a team) has been a godsend, Patrick Mahomes has looked mostly terrific coming off injury, and KC's defense is allowing the second-fewest points per game. But they haven't faced a battering ram of a schedule so far, and six of their next eight games are on the road, so we are going to find out just how real they are over the next two months. 2. Bills Buffalo hits the bye week in great shape at 5-1, but there have been some close-shave victories (and a home loss to the Patriots) among them. Josh Allen has been mostly tremendous in leading the NFL's top-scoring offense, but he's also had to do most of the heavy lifting at times. The run defense has shown improvement from a year ago, but virtually every other aspect of the defense as a whole could use improvement. It will be interesting to see if general manager Brandon Beane can make any personnel improvements on that side of the ball prior to the trade deadline. 3. Jaguars The Jaguars have backed up their 13-win season with a strong 4-2 mark to start this year, although losses to the Broncos and Texans both featured second-half breakdowns after holding fourth-quarter leads. On the whole, Jacksonville has performed like a playoff-caliber team, with Trevor Lawrence playing well and Travis Hunter starting to impact games in more ways. The remaining schedule looks favorable on the surface, with the lowest opponent win percentage (.409), and yet seven of the final 11 games are away from home. 4. Browns This season's early darlings, who incredibly are likely a dropped punt snap away from being 5-1, are 2-0 in the division with wins over the Steelers and Ravens. Deshaun Watson has been functional on the whole but especially good in second halves. This remains a low-scoring offense (17.7 ppg) with pass-protection issues and a lack of run-game punch. Cleveland's defense has been on the rise, keeping four of the past five opponents to 19 points or fewer, but the Browns will have to find ways to make life easier on themselves with all four AFC North teams currently over .500. 5. Patriots The season started on a sour note, as Drake Maye struggled and the defense could do only so much to help out. The arrow has pointed up in recent weeks as Maye has gotten back on track and A.J. Brown has returned to the lineup, although his first full game in Week 6 was forgettable. Keeping pace with the Bills will be tough with four of the next five games away from home and some high-profile matchups left, including current unbeatens Minnesota and Kansas City in Weeks 14 and 15. 6. Broncos There's a lot to figure out on offense, where play-calling duties have already shifted from Davis Webb back to Sean Payton — and the early results have been even worse than before. On the season, the Broncos average a league-worst 4.6 yards per play. Denver's two losses, both on the road, have each been by double digits. Its four victories have all been one-score affairs. Defensively, the Broncos have lived and died on sacks and turnovers but have been leaky against the run, with poor tackling. Payton has a tough, competitive team, but until Bo Nix and the offense get going, they're also an incomplete one. 7. Steelers Aaron Rodgers has 12 TD passes and is on pace for his best passing totals since his MVP campaign in 2021, but he's averaging a turnover per game. The Steelers needed overtime to beat the Buccaneers and lost their other two road outings. With the Ravens and Bengals right on their heels, the Steelers will need to continue forcing turnovers on defense and cut back on them on offense. Their margin for error feels a little slim, even with the 4-2 start to the season. NFC Brock Purdy has been a big reason why the San Francisco 49ers are 6-0 to start the season. Lachlan Cunningham via Getty Images 1. 49ers Even after Monday's scare against the Commanders, it's been hard to argue with much of what we've seen from the Niners this season. They're 6-0, including 3-0 in the division with head-to-head road victories over the Rams and Seahawks, the presumed NFC West faves entering the season. Brock Purdy is playing at an MVP level, and the defense has been improved, even if there's a need for more big plays. One thing to watch: Mike Evans' health. The 49ers are a different team with and without him on the field. Losing him, on top of all their other injuries, would be a major blow to their No. 1 seed chances. 2. Vikings They're 5-0 but ripe for questions given the state of the offense right now. Kyler Murray is back under center after missing parts of two games, and they've had the bye week to make adjustments, but they'll need to find ways to be more explosive. Brian Flores' defense is absolutely smothering opponents, averaging two forced turnovers per game and giving up 513 pass yards the past four games combined, but can this unit carry the team all season? There's also the matter of the remaining strength of schedule, which is a whopping .572, with several tough opponents ahead. 3. Panthers Bryce Young is off to a terrific start, and the Panthers' offense is starting to resemble a pretty interesting unit. Chuba Hubbard has anchored the run game, and the offensive line hasn't been the concern area some thought it might be. After allowing 59 points in the opener, the Panthers have settled down a bit, giving up only 64 in the four games since. There's still room for improvement on that side, but the arrow is pointing up. With more home games (seven) than road games (five) remaining, and amid a weaker NFC South, there's a pretty good runway for the Panthers to make the postseason two straight years. 4. Giants The move to start J.J. McCarthy feels like an inflection point on the season. The Giants currently lead the morass that is the NFC East, but they're going to need better QB play consistently from here on out to hang onto the division lead. All three wins have come at home, and they have yet to win on the road, which is where the next two games are, with the bye in between. John Harbaugh has helped make the team more competitive, but the defense needs to make more big plays to keep them ahead of a weakened division. 5. Packers The Packers' season looked wayward after the 1-2 start, but three straight victories have changed the trajectory, especially with Jordan Love starting to take command of the offense. item.title: What did Bruno Fernandes say about Man United tactics? Red Devils captain questions Michael Carrick after Como loss
item.description: What did Bruno Fernandes say about Man United tactics? Red Devils captain questions Michael Carrick after Como loss originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has come under fire for the team's extremely poor start to the 2026/27 season. Sitting 13th in the Premier League table with just one win in seven league matches, the Red Devils have won just two games across all competitions this season, beaten most recently 4-1 by Como in an embarrassing road loss that piled on the pressure. After the match, things become even more toxic as the United captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to question his manager's tactical approach to the match, seeming to point the finger at the head coach when asked what went wrong in the match. That has brought criticism upon both Carrick and Fernandes himself, as the behavior has been deemed unfit for a club captain. MORE: What went wrong for Michael Carrick at Man United? What did Bruno Fernandes say about Michael Carrick tactics? After the defeat to Como, Man United captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to openly question the manager's tactics in the game. "It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence," he said. Asked directly whether Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: "That's on the manager and staff to see it, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable." Man United have largely not been a high-pressing team throughout Michael Carrick's tenure as permanent manager this season. MORE: All the latest Man United news Michael Carrick responds to Bruno Fernandes criticism Manchester United boss Michael Carrick responded to the criticism of the tactics from his captain. In his post-match press conference, Carrick was asked about his captain's choice of words, and defended his approach, saying that they tried to press at one point, and conceded a goal from it. Michael Carrick responded to Bruno Fernandes' post-match comments criticising the tactics. https://t.co/RpJLlaEstb — Match of the Day (@BBCMOTD) October 21, 2026

item.title: Ole Miss vs. Texas prediction, odds, pick for SEC clash in Week 8
item.description: Ole Miss vs. Texas prediction, odds, pick for SEC clash in Week 8 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Texas Longhorns have lost two straight games and look to rebound as they host Ole Miss. It is time to continue the NCAA Football odds series with an Ole Miss-Texas prediction and pick. Ole Miss comes into the game 5-1 on the season. It was a tight first game as Ole Miss faced off with Louisville in Nashville, Tennessee. Ole Miss hit a field goal as time expired to win 41-38. After knocking off Charlotte, they hosted former head coach Lane Kiffin and LSU. Trinidad Chamliss ran in a 14-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter to give Ole Miss the 32-24 victory. The next week would be a complete disaster, visiting Florida. They fell 52-28. Since then, the Rebels have defeated Vanderbilt and Missouri. It was c omplete domination for Ole Miss against Missouri, winning 31-3 . Meanwhile, Texas opened the season 4-0. After taking out Texas State, they had a massive comeback victory over Ohio State, winning 24-23. They would then defeat UTSA and Tennessee on the road. In the Red River Rivalry, Arch Manning struggled late. Texas had a ten-point lead at the half, but multiple late Manning turnovers led to a 27-24 win for Oklahoma. Last time out was another difficult game for Texas. Texas once again had a ten-point lead, this time facing Florida. Once again, they let their opponent back in the game. Florida held the lead to 27-17 until Manning found Cam Coleman for a touchdown, but they could not score again, and Texas lost 27-14. Ole Miss has beaten Texas just one other time, defeating the Longhorns in the 1958 Sugar Bowl. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) This will be just the eighth meeting between the two schools. The last time they met was in 2013, and Ole Miss won 44-23, but that win was vacated. Ole Miss has beaten Texas just one other time, defeating the Longhorns in the 1958 Sugar Bowl. Odds provided by DraftKings Ole Miss vs. Texas Odds Ole Miss: +3.5 (-118) Texas: -3.5 (-102) Over: 54.5 (-105) Under: 54.5 (-115) Ole Miss vs. Texas Key Injuries Ole Miss- RB Kewan Lacy (Probable), RB Makhi Frazier (Probable), OL Patrick Kutas (Probable) Texas- DL Justus Terry (Probable), OL Jordan Coleman (Probable), OL Jaydon Chatman (Out), WR Kaliq Lockett (Out), RB Hollywood Smothers (Questionable), EDGE Colin Simmons (Out) Ole Miss vs. Texas Betting Trends – The Rebels are 3-3 against the spread this year, but have covered in two straight. – Ole Miss is 11 against the spread on the road, and 1-1 as the underdog. – The over is 3-3 for Ole Miss this year, including both times on the road. – Texas is 1-5 against the spread and has failed to cover in five straight. – Texas is 1-3 against the spread at home this year. – The under has hit in four of six games for the Longhorns this year, and three of four at home Keys to Ole Miss vs. Texas matchup For Ole Miss, it is all about keeping on schedule. This year, when the offense has been able to keep its rhythm, it has been elite. They are ninth in the nation in points per game, 25th in third-down conversions, and 21st in yards per game. It is not a perfectly balanced offense either. They are 116th in the nation in rush play percentage, while sitting 23rd in pass play percentage, but the disparity works. Trinidad Chambliss is the reason why. He has passed for 1,676 yards this year while having 14 touchdowns and just four interceptions. He has also scored six times on the ground. Meanwhile, Kewan Lacy has been great when in the lineup, running for 352 yards and five scores. If they can keep Texas off balance, the lack of Colin Simmons in the lineup will show, and Ole Miss will put up major points. On defense, they have to put pressure on Arch Manning. Manning has already thrown five interceptions and been sacked 17 times. Many of his mistakes have come under pressure, and Ole Miss is great at getting pressure on the quarterback. Texas is 112th in the nation in sack rate currently, while 90th in interception rate. Blake Purchase has been solid this year. He has 3.5 sacks and a forced fumble, while Will Echoles has been great at creating pressure up the middle. For Texas, they have to put Arch Manning in positive situations. That starts with the run game. With Hollywood Smothers potentially out for this game, that will put pressure on Raleek Brown. He has run for 265 yards and five touchdowns. Meanwhile, Manning has plenty of weapons to get the ball too if he has time. Ryan Wingo has been great this year, bringing in 26 receptions for 345 yards and three scores. Meanwhile, Cam Coleman has been a big play threat all year. He has 20 receptions for 336 yards and six touchdowns. Still, Manning needs time and protection to get the ball to Coleman. On defense, losing Colin Simmons for the game is a massive blow. He has 10.5 sacks this year with two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery. They have to contain Trinidad Chambliss in this game, and that will be difficult without Simmons. It is going to start with Justus Terry. The interior defensive lineman needs to get a solid push to put Chambliss into quick decisions. They also need to force some turnovers. Texas has just .8 takeaways per game this year, and if they are not going to create short fields, it is going to be a difficult day for Texas. Ole Miss vs. Texas Prediction and Pick The Longhorns have struggled to cover the spread this year, going just 1-5 against the spread and failing to cover in five straight games. Further, they are coming off back-to-back losses, and Arch Manning has been struggling. Texas is also without their best defensive player. Meanwhile, Ole Miss is riding high. They just shut down Missouri and held their potent running game to under 50 yards. The line has this set up to be a one-score game, and since the start of 2024, Ole Miss is 10-1 in one-score contests, including 2-0 this year. The road environment may be difficult for Ole Miss, but the Rebels get the win in this one. Further, Texas will struggle to score as the Rebels shut down the big plays, leading to the under hitting. Final Ole Miss vs. Texas Prediction and Pick: Ole Miss +3.5 (-118) and Under 54.5 (-115) Related: Indiana vs. Michigan prediction, odds, pick for college football Week 8 Related: LeBron James, Joel Embiid odds highlight fraught nature of 76ers’ superteam experiment

item.title: Como 4-1 Manchester United: Red Devils humiliated in Italy
item.description: Como 4-1 Manchester United: Red Devils humiliated in Italy Michael Carrick’s injury-plagued side continued to fall short after a 4-1 thrashing in the Champions League by Cesc Fàbregas’ Como. Nico Paz opened the scoring within a few minutes, which proved to be the only goal of the first half. Anastasios Douvikas added a second early in the second half before Paz inflicted further damage, scoring Como’s third within an hour. Jacobo Ramón added insult to injury for Michael Carrick’s side as he made it 4-0 with 15 minutes to go. Joshua Zirkzee scored a consolation goal in added time as Como ran out comfortable winners. As it happened Nico Paz kicked things off early for Como with an immaculate finish in the third minute. Harry Maguire and Matthijs de Ligt were caught too deep in the Como box, allowing the Argentine ample time to take a perfectly placed shot and put the home side ahead. Manchester United could hardly string a pass together for much of the first half, with the absence of a number of defensive players and midfielders painfully noticeable. Como pressed high consistently, and United lacked the physicality to fight back with any kind of impact. Michael Carrick made half-time substitutions, taking off Andrey Santos and Matheus Cunha for Carlos Baleba and Amad Diallo, but his efforts proved futile as a perfectly executed one-touch sequence from the halfway line allowed Nico Paz to play in Anastasios Douvikas to flick the ball into the net for Como’s second. The night would only continue to worsen for Carrick and his men, already shrouded in recent controversy, as Nico Paz made a tidy run and slotted a shot round Senne Lammens with ease to score his second goal of the night and put his side 3-0 up. A dejected Bruno Fernandes was substituted for Joshua Zirkzee after 67 minutes with little complaint. Less than 10 minutes later, Kaiki took advantage of United’s weak defence, as a slow Maguire and an out-of-practice de Ligt left Jacobo Ramón unmarked following a fast counter-attack to give Como a four-goal cushion. Zirkzee did manage to have a small impact from the bench, scoring a consolation goal for his side in the 91st minute from a high cross by Amad, but the consolation goal did little to soften the blow. The win and high scoreline leave Como in sixth, above Manchester City on goal difference, with one more goal scored. Manchester United sit in 20th, with one win and two losses from three games.

item.title: 0 tackles, 67% duels lost, 1 error: Noussair Mazraoui appeared to down tools vs Como
item.description: 0 tackles, 67% duels lost, 1 error: Noussair Mazraoui appeared to down tools vs Como Manchester United were thrashed 4-1 by Champions League newcomers Como in what was another horror away performance from Michael Carrick’s team this season. The head coach’s bizarre tactical calls and lack of coaching were clearly on display while Cesc Fabregas had his team purring on the night. United skipper Bruno Fernandes even called out Carrick after the game as the atmosphere around the club gets toxic by the minute. The lack of effort on the part of certain players was concerning with Noussair Mazraoui downing tools right from the first whistle. Noussair Mazraoui downed tools The normally consistent Moroccan was abysmal on the night, failing to make a single tackle while losing 67% of all his duels. That was not all. The versatile full-back also made an error that led to a shot and was dribbled past once. He did complete two clearances and recovered the ball back on three occasions. match stats On the ball, the former Bayern Munich man was equally poor, failing to find a teammate with 50% of his long ball attempts. One cross found its mark while the Morocco international failed to beat his man on both occasions. The 28-year-old did not attempt a single shot, nor did he manage a key pass (all stats via sofascore ). Noussair Mazraoui not playing for his United future He started as the left-sided full-back and Nico Paz ran at him and he did not put up much of a challenge. Carrick opted to switch him to the opposite flank for the start of the second half, but that did little to change the outcome. There was speculation regarding his future in the summer , but the ex-Ajax ace opted to stay at Old Trafford. But with INEOS planning a defensive overhaul next summer and given his current form, the likelihood of Noussair Mazraoui staying seems remote at best. Feature image Marco Luzzani via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains
item.description: A rush of new data centers could bring air pollution roaring back to levels not seen since the 2000s in Texas, which has become ground zero for the physical infrastructure behind generative AI. New and proposed data centers are demanding a tremendous amount of electricity. How developers and utilities meet that demand - with gas turbines or renewable energy - will determine just how dirty things will get. So far, though, things are looking grim. Tech companies and data center developers are devising new ways to get enough electricity, including building out their own power sources. But if all planned data center projects were to plug into … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Ravens’ Trenton Simpson Makes Bold Statement About Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey Ahead of Bengals Clash
item.description: The Baltimore Ravens have had plenty to sort out on defense this season, particularly in a secondary preparing for one of its toughest assignments. Facing the Cincinnati Bengals means dealing with two receivers who can punish even a small mistake, and there won’t be much room for hesitation when Joe Burrow starts looking downfield. The Ravens have talent at cornerback; however, Sunday will put that confidence to a serious test. They need their defensive backs to hold up in coverage long enough for the pass rush to make an impact, and linebacker Trenton Simpson has made it clear which teammates he trusts to handle the challenge. Trenton Simpson backs Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey against Bengals stars Nov 16, 2025; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (12) is sacked by Baltimore Ravens linebacker Trenton Simpson (32) during the fourth quarter at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images Simpson is backing Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey in the team’s upcoming game against the Bengals. As per a report from ESPN correspondent Jamison Hensley, Simpson feels that Ravens’ cornerbacks are well equipped to play against the Bengals’ receivers in their upcoming game. “This is the game where you challenge Ja’Marr Chase, you challenge Tee Higgins. And I like our guys. I love Nate Wiggins and I love Marlon Humphrey. And I believe that those are the two guys for that opportunity. And I think they’re going to do a great job.” Ravens linebacker Trenton Simpson on the matchup between Baltimore's CBs vs. Bengals WRs: "This is the game where you challenge Ja'Marr Chase, you challenge Tee Higgins. item.title: Gerry Dulac Shuts Down Steelers Trade Rumors After Marquez Valdes-Scantling Signing
item.description: The Pittsburgh Steelers have been attempting to mend their receiving corps after a number of players were injured over the past few days. Marquez Valdes-Scantling is now back with the Steelers, reuniting with his quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, and head coach, Mike McCarthy , although his signing has left fans wondering whether this is a stopgap or if there will be another trade before the deadline. The injured reserve is occupied by two receivers, while the offense still needs to find its consistency. The signing means yet another player is familiar with the team, but it doesn’t mean the front office is prepared to spend more. Gerry Dulac Downplays Steelers Trade Rumors Following MVS Reunion Aug 11, 2026; Woodland Hills, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling (11) reacts during a joint practice against the Los Angeles Rams at the Rams Practice Facility. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Steelers are not expected to acquire another wide receiver via trade after signing MVS, according to Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. “No. And not after signing MVS [Marquez Valdes-Scantling]. They’re just trying to apply band-aids for now till their receivers come back. ” Gerry Dulac says the Steelers won't be trading for a WR: “No. And not after signing MVS [Marquez Valdes-Scantling]. They’re just trying to apply band-aids for now till their receivers come back.” #Steelers #NFL — Steelers Depot 7⃣ (@Steelersdepot) October 21, 2026 That answer will likely disappoint fans hoping the Steelers would make a more substantial move. With the loss of Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson to injured reserve, and with Ben Skowronek battling an injury, Rodgers does not have many dependable players to choose from, especially in situations where he needs to play catch-up. Valdes-Scantling may not be a significant improvement on what Rodgers has, but he certainly brings a certain amount of familiarity with him. This is because Valdes-Scantling played under Rodgers with the Green Bay Packers between 2018 and 2021. In five games with them in 2025, the receiver caught 10 passes for 80 yards and a touchdown. Those numbers hardly suggest a major offensive solution; however, the timing of his return matters. Rodgers already knows how MVS operates , and McCarthy coached him during his rookie season with the Packers. That shared history could help the receiver settle in faster than someone arriving from an entirely different system. The Steelers may also need him sooner than expected. Ray Fittipaldo recently suggested on 93.7 The Fan that Valdes-Scantling could be considered for Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris. Pittsburgh barely used Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson in the passing game against Tampa Bay, leaving room for the newly signed veteran to compete for snaps. item.title: ‘You Gotta Discipline Him’ — Rob Gronkowski Offers Blunt Advice to Bills After C.J. Gardner-Johnson’s Bizarre On-Field Antics
item.description: A controversial incident occurred on Sunday, October 18, involving C.J. Gardner-Johnson. The Buffalo Bills secured a 33-30 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, but Gardner-Johnson’s ejection left the team without an important defensive player during a closely contested game. Gardner-Johnson joined the Bills during the offseason and brought experience and intensity to the team’s defense. However, his latest actions have placed his conduct under scrutiny. Dec 13, 2025; Inglewood, CA, USA; Rob Gronkowski watches the LA bowl between the Boise State Broncos and the Washington Huskies at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Rob Gronkowski Urges Bills To Discipline C.J. Gardner-Johnson In a recent episode of The Gronk and Jules Show, former NFL tight end Rob Gronkowski shared his views on the controversy surrounding Gardner-Johnson and how teams should respond when players cross the line. He said: “C.J. Gardner-Johnson, you gotta discipline him in every way possible. Yes, the NFL is gonna discipline him first. We saw after last year in the opening game with the Philadelphia Eagles and their defensive tackle when he spit on Dak Prescott. Like, that’s not allowed. Like, I thought the spitting would be done in the NFL after that example with Jalen Carter. I don’t see why a player would do that. It’s stuck in everyone’s mind that’s so unnecessary. If I’m the Buffalo Bills, I’m disciplining him big time. I wouldn’t wanna like, kick him off the team or anything. That’s going to hurt your team in the long run. He is a good player. So just discipline him.” The head coach of the franchise has expressed disappointment, emphasizing that the team’s discipline must improve and that such behavior cannot be accepted. Although Gardner-Johnson acknowledged his mistake after the game, admitting that he had allowed his emotions to get the better of him and hurt his team, he also apologized publicly and accepted responsibility for his inappropriate actions. Gronkowski’s comments highlight the balance teams must maintain between holding players accountable and protecting their overall performance. While Gardner-Johnson’s experience and defensive abilities make him a valuable asset, his actions can create unnecessary challenges for the coaching staff. Discipline is particularly important in close games, where losing a key player can affect defensive matchups and force teammates to take on additional responsibilities. For Buffalo, the focus will be on ensuring that Gardner-Johnson learns from the incident and avoids similar mistakes in the future. The Bills will need their players to remain focused and composed as they continue competing throughout the NFL season. Although Gardner-Johnson has apologized for his actions, this incident serves as an important lesson that professionalism must be maintained regardless of how difficult a situation becomes. item.title: College Football WR Rankings Week 8: Jesse Legree Takes No. 1 Over Malachi Toney, Jeremiah Smith
item.description: College Football WR Rankings: Jesse Legree Takes No. 1 Over Malachi Toney, Jeremiah Smith Jeremiah Smith and Malachi Toney have spent much of the season in the Heisman Trophy conversation, but neither owns the highest PFN WR Impact grade entering the second half of 2026. That distinction belongs to Oregon State true freshman Jesse Legree, whose first seven college games have produced one of the most remarkable starts by a receiver in recent memory. Legree leads a top five that also includes Toney, Smith, Rutgers standout KJ Duff, and Northwestern’s Griffin Wilde. PFN college football analyst Max Chadwick broke down the five highest-graded receivers in the country based on PFN’s WR Impact metric. The model weighs receiving production alongside opportunity, efficiency, yards after the catch, and strength of schedule rather than simply ranking players by raw yardage. Here are the five highest-graded wide receivers in college football entering the second half of the season. 5) Griffin Wilde, Northwestern PFN WR Impact Grade: 92.6 Griffin Wilde doesn’t have the gaudy counting stats of some of the receivers ahead of him, but his efficiency has made him an important part of Northwestern’s surprising start. Wilde has caught 30 of his 36 targets for 482 yards and three touchdowns through six games. His 83.3% catch rate is easily the best among the five receivers on this list, and he’s averaging 4.8 yards after the catch per reception. Chadwick pointed to Wilde as another beneficiary of Northwestern’s offensive improvement. Quarterback Aidan Chiles has emerged as one of PFN’s five highest-graded quarterbacks, and the combination has helped turn an offense that entered the season with modest expectations into one capable of supporting a ranked team. Wilde had his most explosive performance of the season before Northwestern’s trip to Michigan State, then followed it with six catches for 57 yards in a 24-21 road victory. His season total may not immediately stand out next to the 700-, 900-, and 1,000-yard receivers ahead of him, but PFN’s grading reflects how consistently productive he has been when the ball comes his way. That’s the distinction Chadwick made with Wilde. The case isn’t built around massive volume. It’s built around doing his job efficiently enough to remain one of the most valuable receivers in the country on a per-opportunity basis. 4) KJ Duff, Rutgers PFN WR Impact Grade: 93.3 Rutgers has struggled to find much consistency offensively this season. PFN college football analyst Max Chadwick broke down the five highest-graded receivers in the country based on PFN’s WR Impact metric. The model weighs receiving production alongside opportunity, efficiency, yards after the catch, and strength of schedule rather than simply ranking players by raw yardage. Here are the five highest-graded wide receivers in college football entering the second half of the season. 5) Griffin Wilde, Northwestern PFN WR Impact Grade: 92.6 Griffin Wilde doesn’t have the gaudy counting stats of some of the receivers ahead of him, but his efficiency has made him an important part of Northwestern’s surprising start. Wilde has caught 30 of his 36 targets for 482 yards and three touchdowns through six games. His 83.3% catch rate is easily the best among the five receivers on this list, and he’s averaging 4.8 yards after the catch per reception. Chadwick pointed to Wilde as another beneficiary of Northwestern’s offensive improvement. Quarterback Aidan Chiles has emerged as one of PFN’s five highest-graded quarterbacks, and the combination has helped turn an offense that entered the season with modest expectations into one capable of supporting a ranked team. Wilde had his most explosive performance of the season before Northwestern’s trip to Michigan State, then followed it with six catches for 57 yards in a 24-21 road victory. His season total may not immediately stand out next to the 700-, 900-, and 1,000-yard receivers ahead of him, but PFN’s grading reflects how consistently productive he has been when the ball comes his way. That’s the distinction Chadwick made with Wilde. The case isn’t built around massive volume. It’s built around doing his job efficiently enough to remain one of the most valuable receivers in the country on a per-opportunity basis. 4) KJ Duff, Rutgers PFN WR Impact Grade: 93.3 Rutgers has struggled to find much consistency offensively this season. KJ Duff has been the exception. Duff has 42 receptions for 741 yards and nine touchdowns through six games, ranking among the national leaders in both receiving yardage and scores. He is averaging 17.6 yards per reception despite playing in an offense that hasn’t received anything close to the level of quarterback play enjoyed by most of the other receivers near the top of PFN’s rankings. That context was central to Chadwick’s evaluation. Northwestern has Chiles playing at a high level. Miami has Darian Mensah. Ohio State had Julian Sayin before his Week 7 injury. Duff has produced while Rutgers has rotated quarterbacks and dealt with considerably less stability at the position. His Week 7 performance against Maryland continued the trend. Duff caught nine passes for 113 yards and two touchdowns in Rutgers’ 37-30 win, giving him his fifth game with at least 78 receiving yards and his fourth multi-touchdown performance of the season. There haven’t been many bright spots for Rutgers, but Duff has continued producing regardless of the circumstances around him. Chadwick believes the lack of high-end quarterback play makes his numbers more impressive, not less. 3) Jeremiah Smith, Ohio State PFN WR Impact Grade: 96.6 Third place in these rankings says much more about the caliber of the top two than it does about anything Jeremiah Smith has failed to accomplish. Smith has 52 receptions for 984 yards and 12 touchdowns through seven games. His 5.3 yards per route run are the best of anyone in PFN’s top five, and his production has placed him squarely in the Heisman Trophy race. Chadwick would have Smith atop his Heisman ballot at this point in the season. The Ohio State junior has already produced games of 217 and 206 receiving yards while scoring multiple touchdowns four times. PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN’s Free CFB Playoff Predictor Indiana managed to limit Smith to four receptions in Week 7, but one of them was the biggest offensive play of Ohio State’s 19-15 win. Smith caught a 38-yard touchdown on fourth-and-1 in the fourth quarter, finishing with 68 yards and his 12th receiving score of the season. The more pressing concern for the second half has nothing to do with Smith. Sayin injured his throwing arm against Indiana, and Ryan Day has said Ohio State’s starting quarterback will miss at least several weeks. Smith has been dominant enough that Chadwick isn’t dropping him because of the change, but producing at the same rate with a backup quarterback would strengthen an already compelling Heisman case. Smith entered 2026 as arguably the most accomplished receiver in the sport and has done nothing to diminish that reputation. Two other players have simply been even better according to PFN’s grading model. 2) Malachi Toney, Miami PFN WR Impact Grade: 96.6 Malachi Toney shares the same 96.6 grade as Smith, with PFN currently placing the Miami sophomore one spot ahead. Toney has caught 50 of 59 targets for 758 yards and eight touchdowns, giving him an 84.7% catch rate while averaging 4.7 yards per route run. He has also remained one of the most versatile offensive weapons in college football, contributing as a runner, passer, and returner in addition to his primary role at receiver. That versatility was on display again against Florida State. Toney caught 11 passes for 154 yards and two touchdowns, added 31 rushing yards, and threw a successful two-point conversion as Miami survived 43-35 in double overtime. The performance was another reminder that Toney’s freshman season wasn’t an isolated breakout. He caught 109 passes for 1,211 yards and 10 touchdowns in 2025, setting Miami single-season records in both receptions and receiving yards. Chadwick considers that one of the best true freshman seasons a wide receiver has produced, trailing only what Smith accomplished at Ohio State in 2024. Toney hasn’t slowed down as a sophomore, and the arrival of Mensah has helped Miami build one of the most productive passing attacks in the country. Toney’s 758 yards don’t match Smith or Legree, but volume alone isn’t driving the PFN rankings. His catch rate, efficiency, and ability to create after the catch have kept him essentially even with Smith in WR Impact through the first half of the season. 1) Jesse Legree, Oregon State PFN WR Impact Grade: 98.1 Jesse Legree arrived at Oregon State as a three-star recruit. Seven games later, he’s the highest-graded wide receiver in college football. The true freshman has 46 receptions for an FBS-leading 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns. He’s averaging 22.6 yards per catch and 4.7 yards per route run while producing 10.5 yards after the catch per reception. Those numbers are even more remarkable given his workload. Legree has drawn 65 targets, seven fewer than Smith, yet he’s the only FBS receiver already over 1,000 yards and has two more touchdown catches than the Ohio State star. DIVE IN: PFN’s Free CFB HQ — Team and Player Stats, Info, and More Legree has also topped 100 receiving yards in every college game he’s played. His eight catches for 108 yards and two touchdowns against Washington State extended that streak to seven games, setting an Oregon State record and making him the first FBS receiver since 2023 to post seven consecutive 100-yard performances. item.title: New Celtics Center Mitchell Robinson Had Harsh Assessment of Debut Game vs. Pistons
item.description: New Celtics Center Mitchell Robinson Had Harsh Assessment of Debut Game vs. Pistons originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Mitchell Robinson wasn't satisfied with his first regular-season game in a Boston Celtics uniform. The new Celtics center made his debut against the Detroit Pistons on Monday, but he wasn't pleased with how he performed, particularly on the boards. Robinson was candid about his struggles, acknowledging that he needed to compete at a higher level. Mitchell Robinson told the Globe he'll be OK after tweaking his ankle but was hard on himself about his performance: “I got my ass kicked on the glass. I can’t have no starts like that. It’s cool to get out there and put on that Boston jersey for the first time in a regular-season game, but overall, I still didn’t do what I needed to do. I gotta compete better. I feel like I didn’t compete at a high level that I normally do and I was kind of slow on a lot of things.” #Celtics #Pistons — gary washburn (@GwashburnGlobe) October 21, 2026 “I got my ass kicked on the glass. I can’t have no starts like that,” Robinson said, per Gary Washburn . “It’s cool to get out there and put on that Boston jersey for the first time in a regular-season game, but overall, I still didn’t do what I needed to do. I gotta compete better. I feel like I didn’t compete at a high level that I normally do and I was kind of slow on a lot of things.” The Celtics brought Robinson in to strengthen their interior presence, making his rebounding and physicality important parts of his role. His self-criticism suggests he knows he has more to give, even after finally getting his first regular-season opportunity in a Boston uniform. Boston will need Robinson to make an impact on the glass as the season progresses. While his debut wasn't what he wanted, he has an opportunity to respond and show what he can bring to the Celtics' frontcourt. item.description: The Charlotte Hornets will open up their season against the Brooklyn Nets at the Barclays Center on Wednesday night. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images How to Watch Charlotte Hornets vs Brooklyn Nets When: Wednesday, October 21, 2026 Time: 7:30 PM ET TV Channel: NBC, WZBJ – WZBJ 24, YES Network Live Stream: Fubo ( try for free ) Charlotte begins its regular season following a 116-98 preseason loss to the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday. Rookie Hannes Steinbach led the Hornets with 19 points, 10 rebounds, and three steals, shooting 7-for-9 from the field. Brandon Miller added 15 points and two blocks, while Christian Anderson contributed 15 points and six assists. Charlotte trailed 79-62 entering the fourth quarter and struggled to overcome Memphis’ balanced offense, finishing its preseason schedule with a 1-4 record as the post-LaMelo Ball era officially begins. Brooklyn enters its season opener after suffering a 144-128 loss to the Miami Heat on Wednesday, ending the preseason with a 3-1 record. Michael Porter Jr. led the Nets with 27 points, connecting on four three-pointers, while Egor Demin added 17 points and Julius Randle contributed 15 points, six rebounds and five assists. Rookie Mikel Brown Jr. scored 15 points in his preseason debut after missing the first three games with an ankle injury. item.title: How to watch New Mexico State vs Sam Houston: Live stream NCAA College Football, TV channel
item.description: New Mexico State travels to Sam Houston as the favorite in a lone Conference USA clash on Wednesday. Sep 12, 2026; Honolulu, Hawaii, USA; New Mexico State Aggies running back James Jones (2) reacts after making a touchdown over the Hawaii Rainbow Warriors during the second quarter at the Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex. Mandatory Credit: Marco Garcia-Imagn Images How to watch New Mexico State vs Sam Houston Date: Wednesday, October 21, 2026 Time: 8 PM EDT Channel: ESPN2 Stream: Fubo ( try for free ) Sam Houston is still chasing a first Conference USA win of the season as it hosts New Mexico State on Wednesday as the college football cycle continues. The midweek matchup pits the 1-5 Bearkats against the 2-4 Aggies, who have back-to-back games against C-USA favorites Jacksonville State and Liberty coming up over the next fortnight. In preparation for those pressure fixtures, head coach Tony Sanchez will hope to go 2-1 in the conference and keep his side in contention for some upward movement in the coming weeks. Sam Houston counterpart Phil Longo may already be fighting for his survival in Texas, meanwhile, having 3-15 with the Bearkats program to date. Both teams are coming off limp defeats in their most recent outings, with Sam Houston falling 16-3 at home to Western Kentucky this time last week. NMSU beat that same opponent 34-13 at the start of October before succumbing 22-3 at FIU and then heading for a bye week. The worrying stat line for Longo’s side is that each of their two Conference USA games so far this season has resulted in a combined six points scored. That could all change on Tuesday if Sam Houston’s superior turnover percentage comes good at Bowers Stadium, though recent form suggests Longo’s second-year Air Raid offense isn’t improving at the required pace. item.description: Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant holds up an identification card while posing for photos during Rockets Media Day in Houston, Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) The Houston Rockets open the 2026-27 NBA season tonight against the Dallas Mavericks at Toyota Center. The opener comes with a later tipoff (7:30 p.m.) and amid construction to the arena. Follow our staff for live updates from the first of 82 regular-season games: How to watch When/where: 7:30 p.m., Toyota Center TV/streaming : Space City Home Network and SCHN+. Radio: 790 AM and 101.7 FM (Spanish) Broadcast change After Vanessa Richardson's departure for ESPN last week, the Rockets are not expected to have a sideline reporter on their TV broadcasts until her replacement is in place. So it'll be a two-person broadcast for the interim with play-by-play man Craig Ackerman and analyst Ryan Hollins on Space City Home Network. - Greg Rajan Can Rockets make NBA Finals? See how NBA scouts and an executive assess Houston's chances to catch San Antonio and Oklahoma City. - Varun Shankar Standards and stakes are higher for Rockets After two straight first-round playoff exits, the standard of success goes up for everybody. "Coaches, players, we're not just trying to make the playoffs," coach Ime Udoka said. "We talked about being competitive and changing the perception in Year One and we did that. So the next steps are to not just make the playoffs but make some noise while you're there." - Varun Shankar Straight shooter Meet the Rockets' new assistant coach, Chip Engelland . item.title: Jon Rahm agrees to part ways with LIV Golf and gives up the remainder of his $300 million-plus deal
item.description: Source: operations@newsimages.co.uk/Depositphotos Jon Rahm’s departure from LIV Golf marks a major turning point for the two-time major champion and the financially troubled league. The Spaniard has reached a separation agreement that allows him to leave behind a contract reportedly worth more than $300 million. In exchange, Rahm is relinquishing his remaining financial claims, including money he could have received under the original deal. The agreement comes after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund withdrew its financial backing and LIV Golf entered bankruptcy proceedings. Rahm’s decision also ends his association with Legion XIII, the franchise he captained throughout his time on the circuit. His exit leaves questions about LIV’s rebuilding plans and the future of its remaining stars. The agreement could also reopen opportunities elsewhere in professional golf. Jon Rahm gives up more than $100 million to leave LIV Golf Rahm and LIV Golf reached their separation agreement in October 2026, ending a partnership that began in December 2023. The agreement releases him from his remaining contractual obligations and allows him to pursue opportunities with other tours, leagues, and sponsors without LIV’s consent. The financial sacrifice is substantial. Court records and reporting indicate that Rahm was believed to be owed more than $100 million under the remainder of his contract. His original LIV agreement was reported to be worth more than $300 million, with some estimates placing the guarantee at approximately $350 million. The agreement also addresses money already owed. LIV’s bankruptcy filings listed Rahm as its largest unsecured creditor, with approximately $7.5 million outstanding when the league filed for Chapter 11 protection in September. Rahm agreed to release his monetary and economic claims against the organization rather than pursue those payments and the remaining contract value. The agreement does not provide monetary compensation to Rahm. Instead, it gives him a contractual break from LIV while restoring important rights associated with his name, image, likeness, and related marks, subject to bankruptcy-court approval. LIV Golf’s financial crisis changed the equation Rahm’s exit unfolded during a period of serious instability for LIV Golf. The league filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund withdrew its financial support, forcing the organization to reconsider its structure and plans for the future. The proposed next phase, referred to as LIV Golf 2.0, became central to Rahm’s decision. During a bankruptcy court hearing on October 7, his attorney, John Beck, said Rahm had independently reviewed the proposed terms and found them unacceptable. Beck confirmed that his client would not participate in the league’s next iteration. The separation agreement followed the announcement, formalizing the end of Rahm’s contractual relationship with LIV. Court approval was scheduled for November 5, m
item.content:encoded: Source: operations@newsimages.co.uk/Depositphotos Jon Rahm’s departure from LIV Golf marks a major turning point for the two-time major champion and the financially troubled league. The Spaniard has reached a separation agreement that allows him to leave behind a contract reportedly worth more than $300 million. In exchange, Rahm is relinquishing his remaining financial claims, including money he could have received under the original deal. The agreement comes after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund withdrew its financial backing and LIV Golf entered bankruptcy proceedings. Rahm’s decision also ends his association with Legion XIII, the franchise he captained throughout his time on the circuit. His exit leaves questions about LIV’s rebuilding plans and the future of its remaining stars. The agreement could also reopen opportunities elsewhere in professional golf. Jon Rahm gives up more than $100 million to leave LIV Golf Rahm and LIV Golf reached their separation agreement in October 2026, ending a partnership that began in December 2023. The agreement releases him from his remaining contractual obligations and allows him to pursue opportunities with other tours, leagues, and sponsors without LIV’s consent. The financial sacrifice is substantial. Court records and reporting indicate that Rahm was believed to be owed more than $100 million under the remainder of his contract. His original LIV agreement was reported to be worth more than $300 million, with some estimates placing the guarantee at approximately $350 million. The agreement also addresses money already owed. LIV’s bankruptcy filings listed Rahm as its largest unsecured creditor, with approximately $7.5 million outstanding when the league filed for Chapter 11 protection in September. Rahm agreed to release his monetary and economic claims against the organization rather than pursue those payments and the remaining contract value. The agreement does not provide monetary compensation to Rahm. Instead, it gives him a contractual break from LIV while restoring important rights associated with his name, image, likeness, and related marks, subject to bankruptcy-court approval. LIV Golf’s financial crisis changed the equation Rahm’s exit unfolded during a period of serious instability for LIV Golf. The league filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund withdrew its financial support, forcing the organization to reconsider its structure and plans for the future. The proposed next phase, referred to as LIV Golf 2.0, became central to Rahm’s decision. During a bankruptcy court hearing on October 7, his attorney, John Beck, said Rahm had independently reviewed the proposed terms and found them unacceptable. Beck confirmed that his client would not participate in the league’s next iteration. The separation agreement followed the announcement, formalizing the end of Rahm’s contractual relationship with LIV. Court approval was scheduled for November 5, meaning the agreement’s final legal status remained subject to the bankruptcy process as of October 21. LIV has explored a potential restructuring, including a proposed investment from BC Partners Credit. However, rebuilding the league requires more than financing; retaining established players is also crucial to its competitive credibility and commercial appeal. Source: operations@newsimages.co.uk/Depositphotos Rahm leaves after three championship seasons Rahm’s departure is especially significant because he was one of LIV Golf’s most successful players. He won the league’s individual season championship in each of his three seasons on the circuit, establishing himself as a central figure in its competitive identity. His move to LIV in late 2023 had been one of the most consequential developments in professional golf’s ongoing divide. At the time, he was the reigning Masters champion and among the sport’s most prominent players, giving the breakaway league a major addition as it competed with established tours. Rahm also captained Legion XIII, the team introduced alongside his arrival. The separation agreement restores his rights to his name, image, and likeness, as well as related marks that include the “Rahmbo” nickname and the Legion XIII name. That arrangement gives Rahm greater control over his identity and commercial interests after his departure. It also separates his future career from the team structure that defined his LIV tenure. The change could influence how Rahm approaches future sponsorships and business opportunities as he determines his next steps in professional golf. Fun fact: Before focusing on golf, Jon Rahm played five sports as a child in Spain: soccer, canoeing, jai alai, golf, and kung fu. What Rahm’s exit means for his next chapter The agreement allows Rahm to pursue opportunities across professional golf, but it does not automatically guarantee reinstatement to the PGA Tour. His return would depend on the tour’s eligibility requirements and any applicable decisions by its leadership. Source: dleindecdp/Depositphotos Rahm had previously declined an opportunity to return through the PGA Tour’s Returning Member Program, which Brooks Koepka used earlier in 2026. The program was described as a one-time offer, leaving uncertainty about what route, if any, might be available to Rahm after his departure from LIV. The DP World Tour remains another important part of his competitive future. Rahm is a two-time major champion and has maintained a connection to European golf, while his eligibility for the four major championships remains separate from his membership status on individual tours. His next steps therefore involve both sporting and administrative considerations. Leaving LIV removes his contractual restrictions, but the precise path back into the PGA Tour’s competitive structure has not been confirmed. TL;DR Jon Rahm and LIV Golf reached a separation agreement in October 2026. Rahm agreed to surrender all monetary claims, including more than $100 million believed to remain on his reported $350 million contract. The agreement restores his name, image, and likeness rights and releases him from LIV contractual obligations. Rahm won the LIV individual championship in each of his three seasons and captured four tournaments on the circuit. His departure follows LIV’s bankruptcy filing after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund withdrew financial support. A return to the PGA Tour is not guaranteed, and the separation agreement was scheduled for court approval on November 5. This article was made with AI assistance and human editing. item.title: Steelers’ Troy Fautanu Shares Key Mindset for Handling Left Tackle Expectations
item.description: Troy Fautanu knows the left tackle position comes with a different level of scrutiny in the Pittsburgh Steelers ; protecting quarterback Aaron Rodgers’ blind side is a major responsibility, and the Steelers need more consistency from a player they selected in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. His recent performances have raised questions; however, Fautanu is not treating the pressure as a reason to second-guess himself. The third-year lineman has had to adjust more than once since arriving in the NFL. That makes his latest comments particularly telling, especially with the Steelers looking for stability up front during a season when its offensive line has already drawn plenty of attention. Troy Fautanu Explains How He Plans To Handle Left Tackle Pressure Jul 23, 2025; Latrobe, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers offensive tackle Troy Fautanu talks to the media at Saint Vincent College. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images On October 21, the offensive tackle acknowledged that moving to left tackle brings added pressure. He also explained why the coaching staff’s decision to trust him with the job gives him confidence when doubts creep in. “For sure, there is the added pressure of playing left tackle, but it also gives me confidence because they have the confidence in me that I was able to do it. Whenever you have those thoughts of doubt or doubt creeps into your mind, sometimes you just have to remember they wouldn’t put me in this important position if they didn’t believe in me.” Troy Fautanu admits there is pressure moving to left tackle: “For sure, there is the added pressure of playing left tackle, but it also gives me confidence because they have the confidence in me that I was able to do it. Whenever you have those thoughts of doubt or doubt creeps… — Blitzburgh (@Blitz_Burgh) October 21, 2026 Fautanu’s point is simple: if the Steelers believe he can handle one of the most demanding positions on the offensive line, he has to trust that judgment himself; however, the challenge now is turning that confidence into steadier performances on the field. His recent numbers explain why the position has become a talking point. Against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on October 18, The Steelers OT allowed four pressures, including a sack and a quarterback hit on Rodgers. His season total climbed to 17 pressures allowed, putting him among the league’s more frequently beaten offensive tackles. Those struggles have come as the Steelers continue to reshape their offensive line under head coach Mike McCarthy. The unit has shown signs of improvement in recent weeks; however, edge protection remains an issue. Fautanu’s transition adds some context . item.title: Four things Washington Commanders must do to make up for Terry McLaurin’s loss
item.description: Dan Quinn said that the Commanders have faced “ a season’s worth of adversity ” in their first six games. The beleaguered head coach is correct. They lost Laremy Tunsil in training camp. Jayden Daniels suffered an elbow dislocation in Week 2 and missed some time. They were down to seventh-round rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis against the Colts. There was also the Week 5 debacle against the New York Giants that turned Quinn’s seat into a five-alarm fire. And the sting of being a failed two-point conversion away from sending Philly to overtime and two fateful failed fourth downs from beating the 49ers. Then came the latest knuckle sandwich. Terry McLaurin’s knee was placed in an air cast and carted off the field against San Francisco after suffering a season-ending torn patellar tendon . I mean, come on. “He brings a lot on and off the field,” Quinn said. “I felt him in so many unique ways this season from training camp to in-season. We do have a deep crew at that position and we’ll lean on several guy to fill the unique role that Terry does.” There’s no replacing a player like McLaurin. There are special players in this league and he is one. The Commanders must triage, evaluate and then decide how to keep the passing game going strong without McLaurin in the pattern. Here’s what they’ll need to make that happen: Stefon Diggs to play like a true No. 1 Stefon Diggs was an elite, frontline receiver is his younger days and remains an effective and impactful presence in the passing game. His career numbers illustrate that with 1,000-yard seasons in each year since 2018 , save two impacted by injury. He understands coverage as well as anyone and always finds ways to get open. Diggs is a rabid competitor and solid leader of the position group and can carry that mantle he was previously sharing with McLaurin. Game days will be key, especially as coverage starts to devote significant effort to stopping him. He should still be able to operate in those settings as he has so many times before. His target share will surely go up. While he’s not as dynamic as he once and he has had some uncharacteristic drops early on, Diggs is the type to step up and assume a major role in this Commanders offense. Reserves must form a McLaurin Voltron McLaurin does so many things well that his deep skill set can’t be replicated by one individual. McLaurin has deep speed. He’s good creating separation. And, as Quinn put it, his “superpower” is making contested catches. The Commanders have a little bit of that in different options, which is why they’ll have to form a McLaurin Voltron. For those not alive in the 1980s, you’ll have to Google that reference. They can do so with Dyami Brown and Luke McCaffrey stretching the field. Rookie Antonio Williams is excellent creating separation. And Treylon Burks has the contested catch ability you’re looking for. Washington must deploy them correctly and scheme towards their strengths. If those guys can do that, the Commanders should
item.content:encoded: Dan Quinn said that the Commanders have faced “ a season’s worth of adversity ” in their first six games. The beleaguered head coach is correct. They lost Laremy Tunsil in training camp. Jayden Daniels suffered an elbow dislocation in Week 2 and missed some time. They were down to seventh-round rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis against the Colts. There was also the Week 5 debacle against the New York Giants that turned Quinn’s seat into a five-alarm fire. And the sting of being a failed two-point conversion away from sending Philly to overtime and two fateful failed fourth downs from beating the 49ers. Then came the latest knuckle sandwich. Terry McLaurin’s knee was placed in an air cast and carted off the field against San Francisco after suffering a season-ending torn patellar tendon . I mean, come on. “He brings a lot on and off the field,” Quinn said. “I felt him in so many unique ways this season from training camp to in-season. We do have a deep crew at that position and we’ll lean on several guy to fill the unique role that Terry does.” There’s no replacing a player like McLaurin. There are special players in this league and he is one. The Commanders must triage, evaluate and then decide how to keep the passing game going strong without McLaurin in the pattern. Here’s what they’ll need to make that happen: Stefon Diggs to play like a true No. 1 Stefon Diggs was an elite, frontline receiver is his younger days and remains an effective and impactful presence in the passing game. Game days will be key, especially as coverage starts to devote significant effort to stopping him. He should still be able to operate in those settings as he has so many times before. His target share will surely go up. While he’s not as dynamic as he once and he has had some uncharacteristic drops early on, Diggs is the type to step up and assume a major role in this Commanders offense. Reserves must form a McLaurin Voltron McLaurin does so many things well that his deep skill set can’t be replicated by one individual. McLaurin has deep speed. He’s good creating separation. And, as Quinn put it, his “superpower” is making contested catches. The Commanders have a little bit of that in different options, which is why they’ll have to form a McLaurin Voltron. For those not alive in the 1980s, you’ll have to Google that reference. They can do so with Dyami Brown and Luke McCaffrey stretching the field. Rookie Antonio Williams is excellent creating separation. And Treylon Burks has the contested catch ability you’re looking for. Washington must deploy them correctly and scheme towards their strengths. If those guys can do that, the Commanders should be fine. If Burks is healthy and available, it’s fair to assume he’ll start and play a ton. Williams can work from anywhere but becomes a weapon inside and should see more targets as well. Chig Okonkwo’s involvement goes (way) up Chig Okonkwo took some time to get revved up in the Commanders offense. An early hamstring set him back and kept him out of Weeks 2-3 . He wasn’t super involved in Week 4 but has been far better since then, with 11 catches for 129 yards on 13 targets over the last two weeks. That’s efficient and explosive production that simply must continue now, to keep some attention off Diggs and be a weapon in the middle of the field. Considering John Bates’ presence as a stout blocker and in-line player allows Okonkwo to work from almost anywhere, giving offensive coordinator David Blough to treat him as a receiver at times. Okonkwo has excellent potential. Now’s the time to realize it. No trades!!!! We’re already seen fans discuss the prospect of adding Brian Thomas Jr. or another talent before the trade deadline to make up for McLaurin’s loss. Absolutely not. This team is not in position to be dealing Day 2 or even higher Day 3 pick right now. They need as many assets as possible to fortify their foundation. As a matter of fact, the Commanders could be sellers if the losing continues after the bye. There’s enough talent on the roster and practice squad to keep going. And, just so we’re on the record here, it’s hard pass on Tyreek Hill (no matter where’s he’s at in his rehab) and Brandon Aiyuk. This team doesn’t need that. Promote Van Jefferson or Jaden Bradley off the practice squad and work with what you’ve got. How can the Commanders keep the passing game going with Terry McLaurin now lost for the season? Let us know in the article comments below .

item.title: Packers Coach Sends Clear Message About Coleman Owen After Cowboys Win
item.description: Special teams coordinator Cam Achord said Tuesday that Coleman Owen is “definitely a guy that we’d like back there” after the practice squad receiver handled punt returns in the Green Bay Packers ‘ 23-13 win over the Dallas Cowboys . Aug 29, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Coleman Owen (9) runs with the ball against the Detroit Lions during the first half at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Green Bay signed Owen to the practice squad on Sept. 30. The Packers elevated him and edge rusher Arron Mosby on Saturday after placing returner Skyy Moore on injured reserve. Moore suffered a high-ankle sprain against the Chicago Bears. The Packers (4-2) play Sunday at the Detroit Lions (3-2). Detroit ranks 11th in punt coverage and seventh in kickoff coverage, one of six teams in the top 11 in both. Cam Achord on Coleman Owen: “Definitely a guy that we’d like back there” The return job for Sunday will be decided Saturday, once the staff knows who is healthy after Friday’s practice, Achord said. “And obviously, he did a really good job,” Achord said. “You know, I mean, we’re back there, I think, 16-yard return. You know, no hesitation in catching the ball or anything like that. He was able to get vertical, so, you know, proved himself really good right there.” The Packers scouted Owen’s catch mechanics before they signed him. “Yeah, no, you watch his college stuff at Ohio, and then you watch all of his NFL stuff when he was in Indy,” Achord said. “You know, his game reps, you know, whether it was a limited number of returns in preseason, whether it was kickoff or punt, you watch every rep. And it’s more so seeing how he’s catching the ball. You know, judging the ball, his catch mechanics.” Since Owen arrived, assistant special teams coach Jeff Koonz has given him extra work on the jugs machine before and after practice, according to Achord. “There’s some things that we’ve worked to improve that, you know, he’s taken great pride in,” Achord said. “He’s done a really good job, so, you know, he’s done a good job for us, and we’re really pleased with him.” The kicks Owen fielded Sunday came in low. “Obviously, that was a line drive, you know, both of them,” Achord said. “So, you know, we talk about being able to handle those line drives and catching them in the air. So that’s a big thing because of that artificial hang time. And didn’t panic, caught the ball square, was able to get vertical.” “I think, you know, obviously the first one we want more than we got there,” Achord continued. “The second one he got out past the 30, so that was good. But he definitely has an element of size, you know, you’ve seen bigger guys go back there. He has the size and he does have that speed. So there’s definitely something to build on. He’s very, very talented. I think he’s got one of the bigger legs in the league, high, high hang times, you know, and that allows the coverage units to get down there any time you’re putting the ball 4.8s, you know, 4.7s up there plus. It allows the gunners outside to factor and then the interior.” “And then kickoff wise they’re playing with their hair on fire,” Achord added. “I mean, they are playing physical, they’re strong, they do a really good job condensing it and squeezing to the ball, so, you know, our guys got to do a good job standing up to their size and physical presence out there. It’s going to be a great challenge.” Kickoff at Ford Field is 3:25 p.m. CT Sunday on FOX. item.title: What Joel Embiid said about perpetual target on 76ers’ back after ruining Knicks’ Ring Night
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images What Joel Embiid said about perpetual target on 76ers’ back after ruining Knicks’ Ring Night appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . NEW YORK — For the first time in years, veteran center Joel Embiid sees potential in the Philadelphia 76ers after spoiling the New York Knicks’ banner night at Madison Square Garden. Embiid knows the 76ers still have a long road ahead. But he’s encouraged by Philadelphia’s early returns after a 106-100 Opening Night win. With All-Star talent led by Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, and LeBron James, the 76ers will be one of the few teams circled on opponents’ proverbial calendars. However, Embiid looks forward to the challenge while the Sixers gradually blossom into a true title contender. “Yeah, but it’s also the Knicks. Give them a lot of credit. The former champions — a great team; their starting 5 is excellent; hard to guard. So, I think you should expect that from the champs,” Embiid said. “Every other team that comes in is going to give you their best, but I don’t think we should focus so much on that. I don’t worry too much about other teams; like tonight, I came out of it. I don’t even think about New York. I just think about us, like, OK, we look good defensively. What can we get better at?” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Yeah, but it’s also the Knicks. Give them a lot of credit. The former champions — a great team… I think you should expect that from the champs. Every other team that comes in is going to give you their best, but I don’t think we should focus so much on that… I just think… pic.twitter.com/kkwXiBJzuX — Josue Pavón (@Joe_Sway) October 21, 2026 For Joel Embiid, the 76ers must evolve into one of the NBA’s best defensive teams this season. For the first time in years, he feels healthy, inspired, and driven to revert to an All-Defensive center in 2026-27. However, if the Sixers want a deep playoff run, monitoring Embiid’s usage will be critical. Perhaps the 2023 MVP’s version of an All-Defensive center in 2027 won’t happen in the literal sense, since he’d have to play at least 65 regular-season games. When the Knicks pulled away with a 10-point lead, LeBron James took over at center for Embiid, helping the 76ers find their stride in the third quarter and eventually build a nine-point lead. James finished with 14 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists. Tyrese Maxey led all scorers with 28 points, and Jaylen Brown finished with 19 points, eight rebounds, and six assists. Embiid finished with a double-double (13 points, 11 rebounds), plus six assists, three blocks, and two steals. The Sixers’ defense nearly held the Knicks to under 100 points, a clear step in the right direction early in the regular season. Related: A closer look at 76ers’ LeBron James dropping F-bombs on heckling Knicks fans at MSG Related: Joel Embiid’s ‘miserable’ confession that shows exactly why Philly needed LeBron James, Jaylen Brown

item.title: Ravens LB Trenton Simpson Predicts Big Game for Trey Hendrickson Against Bengals
item.description: Trey Hendrickson won’t have to wait long for his first shot at the team he spent five seasons terrorizing. The Baltimore Ravens brought the veteran pass rusher in to make life miserable for opposing quarterbacks, and a divisional matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals gives him a chance to do exactly that. His former teammates know what he can do; however, the Ravens locker room is already expecting something special. Hendrickson has had a stop-and-start beginning to his Ravens career, with an injury keeping him out for part of the season. Now, with the Bengals coming to town on Sunday, one teammate has made a bold call about what could happen next. Trenton Simpson Expects Trey Hendrickson To Make The Bengals Pay Injured Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) talks on the bench with injured defensive end Trey Hendrickson (91) in the second quarter of the NFL Week 12 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the New England Patriots at Paycor Stadium in downtown Cincinnati on Sunday, Nov. 23, 2025. The Ravens linebacker Trenton Simpson is predicting a multi-sack performance from Hendrickson against the Bengals, according to ESPN reporter Jamison Hensley , who shared Simpson’s comments on October 21. The linebacker did not hide his excitement about seeing the veteran face his former team. Ravens linebacker Trenton Simpson is predicting a multi-sack game for Trey Hendrickson, who is facing his former team in the Bengals. “I’m calling it,” Simpson said. pic.twitter.com/r02Sdm3p0p — Jamison Hensley (@jamisonhensley) October 21, 2026 Simpson pointed to what he’s watched from Hendrickson during practice, particularly the way he gets off the ball and attacks opposing blockers. Those details have convinced him that a big afternoon could be coming. This is certainly a safe bet, particularly against the Bengals, who have Joe Burrow as their starting quarterback. Hendrickson played for five seasons with the Bengals team and emerged as one of the league’s most feared edge rushers. He was the top sack leader in the NFL during the year 2024, and the Bengals team knows for sure what it means to face Hendrickson without any interference. Hendrickson showed some of his abilities even before playing against the Bengals. The Ravens saw Hendrickson play again on October 18 against the Cleveland Browns, where he recorded one sack and pressured the quarterback despite the Ravens losing 13-10. The reunion also carries some intrigue beyond the matchup itself. Hendrickson’s departure from the Bengals f ollowed a contract dispute; however, there is no public indication that he’s treating Sunday’s game as a personal revenge mission. Veteran defensive lineman Calais Campbell a cknowledged that facing an old team can bring extra motivation while making clear that Hendrickson tends to keep his thoughts to himself. As for Cincinnati, the challenge will be containing a pass rusher who knows the division and has plenty of experience against the Bengals’ offense. Extra protec
