item.title: New England Patriots: Get Brutal News on $48 Million Starter
item.description: Injuries have plagued the New England Patriots’ interior offensive line this season, as they will be on their second left guard and fourth right guard. Ben Brown exited the fourth quarter of Week 6 with a knee injury. Brown was estimated as a non-participant, prompting the Patriots to rule him out for Thursday Night Football against the Bears. Matt Pryor will get the start at right guard. The New England Patriots get brutal news on $48 million starter Sep 15, 2024; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; New York Jets guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (75) during pregame warmups against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Alijah Vera-Tucker exited the second quarter of last week’s game with a hamstring injury. Vera-Tucker was estimated as a non-participant, prompting the Patriots to rule him out as well. This will be the first game he’s missed this season and the 18th over the past two seasons. Former Vikings’ sixth-round pick Walter Rouse is expected to make his starting debut at left guard. What about their veteran RT? Jun 10, 2025; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel (center) and offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels (r) work with center Garrett Bradbury (65), offensive tackle Mike Onwenu (71) and offensive tackle Morgan Moses (76) during minicamp held in the WIN Field House at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Morgan Moses suffered a foot injury during the second quarter. Moses was estimated as a limited participant and is officially questionable. Rookie first-round pick Caleb Lomu will start at right tackle if the veteran offensive lineman cannot play. Lomu has served as the swing tackle, filling in at left tackle for Will Campbell in Week 5 and at right tackle for Moses in Weeks 2, 3, and 6, while also seeing time as an extra offensive lineman in jumbo formations. item.title: Hal Steinbrenner Reveals Whether Yankees Still Have 'World Series Or Bust' Mindset
item.description: New York Yankees The New York Yankees go into every season with high expectations, and for fans, it has come to be known as "World Series or bust" every season. There was a point in time where the Yankees were the favorites to win it all every year. They are still contenders going into every season, but their championship drought has reached 17 seasons. Owner Hal Steinbrenner was asked if the Yankees still have a "World Series or bust" mindset. "That's absolutely what we expect," Steinbrenner said during his end-of-season press conference on Wednesday. "That is our mission. That is our goal. Yes, we failed at the goal this year, but that is always our goal, which is why we put so much effort and resources into the roster every offseason to field a team that can accomplish that. And I certainly believe we had that team this year. It just didn't pan out." The Yankees had one of the best pitching staffs in baseball, headlined by likely American League Cy Young Award winner Cam Schlittler. Their offense featured All-Stars Ben Rice and Cody Bellinger. They were without Aaron Judge for most of the season, but they still had a very good team. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! However, their team fell short in October, and that's what ultimately matters. Steinbrenner, Brian Cashman and Aaron Boone will now be responsible for making the necessary fixes to their team in order to get over the hump. They have one of the best players ever in Judge, and have failed to win a championship with him. For starters, he needs to be healthy, but he also needs to have a supporting cast that shows up when it matters. This year, Rice and Bellinger were great, but without Judge, the Yankees never really stood a chance. Next year, they will once again have a roster full of stars, but they have some clear holes they need to address. Third base and second base will be areas of focus this offseason for sure. item.title: The stats don’t lie: Bayern Munich and Arsenal battled to a stalemate
item.description: (Photo by Stuart Franklin - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) | UEFA via Getty Images Bayern Munich may have settled for a 2-2 draw against Arsenal, but the underlying numbers suggest Vincent Kompany’s side had plenty of opportunities to leave with all three points. Despite having just 46% possession compared to Arsenal’s 54%, Bayern Munich generated the greater attacking threat, finishing with 2.51 expected goals (xG) against Arsenal’s 1.40. The German champions also recorded 29 touches in the opposition box, compared to Arsenal’s 21, and created four big chances, twice as many as their opponents. Match stats pic.twitter.com/vWZU0dlMEs — Bayern & Germany (@iMiaSanMia) October 21, 2026 The problem? Bayern Munich missed two of those big chances. Against elite opposition in the Champions League, that kind of wastefulness can be costly, and it ultimately contributed to a result that will leave the Bavarians wondering what might have been. The shot count was nearly identical, with Bayern Munich recording 13 attempts to Arsenal’s 14. Both teams managed five shots on target, suggesting that the difference was not necessarily volume, but the quality of the opportunities created. Arsenal dominated possession and completed more passes, but Bayern Munich was more dangerous when attacking. Kompany’s side also won the battle for touches in the penalty area and created more clear-cut opportunities. There are positives to take from this performance, particularly against one of Europe’s strongest sides. However, Bayern Munich will know that creating chances is only half the job. The bottom line — Bayern Munich had the better opportunities, but failing to capitalize on them meant settling for a draw when three points were there for the taking. Against Arsenal, the margins are razor-thin. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: New, improved notifications system! item.title: Merab Dvalishvili’s coach shares worrying update ahead of UFC 333
item.description: UFC 333 is just three days away, and the co-main event is the card’s most intriguing fight. The trilogy between bantamweight champion Petr Yan and former champ Merab Dvalishvili had to happen. Yan and Dvalishvili are 1-1 against each other, with both fighters winning by dominant unanimous decisions. Dvalishvili enters the third fight on a layoff, having not fought since his last bout against Yan in December 2025, attempting to defend his bantamweight title for the fourth time in one calendar year, a feat never accomplished before. MORE: UFC 333: Alexander Volkanovski vs. Movsar Evloev, main card predictions Aside from Yan’s success on the feet and takedown defense, Dvalishvili looked like he had lost a step, like the activity was catching up to him. Frankly, that makes sense. There’s a reason no one has ever defended a UFC title four times in one year. Now, close to a year removed from competition, Dvalishvili should be amped up and ready. However, another factor to watch ahead of his trilogy against Yan is his return. Back in April of 2026, Dvalishvili was kneed during a sparring session and broke his nose. That injury was aggravated again in a wrestling match against UFC legend Frankie Edgar. A lingering nose injury is a major concern for any sport, and Dvalishvili’s coach’s latest comments aren’t very reassuring. Ray Longo says Merab Dvalishvili’s nose isn’t fixed Dec 6, 2025; Las Vegas, Nevada, UNITED STATES; Merab Dvalishvili fights Petr Yan during UFC 323 at T-Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Stephen R. Sylvanie-Imagn Images; Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Head coach of the Serra-Longo gym, most notably cornered Dvalishvili and Aljamain Sterling, Ray Longo gave an update on his prize pupil. Longo is a recurring guest on the Anik & Florian Podcast, hosted by UFC play-by-play commentator Jon Anik and former UFC fighter Kenny Florian. When talking with the co-hosts about Dvalishvili’s nose, Longo was as blunt as can be. “He’s going to get hit in that nose, and that nose looks like it’s going to bleed. He chose not to have it fixed before the fight.” Safe to say the Yan vs. Merab trilogy fight is gonna be a bloody one 🤣 Merab’s longtime coach Ray Longo updates Jon Anik and Kenny Florian on the status of Merab’s nose heading into UFC 333 and what to expect. Full Episode on the Anik & Florian Podcast YouTube! pic.twitter.com/bheCwnkMqA — Anik & Florian Podcast (@anikflorianpod) October 21, 2026 As soon as Longo said that, Anik was clearly astonished, looking more concerned about the nose than Longo. The other piece of this that’s so weird is Longo mentioning that in the first place, on a podcast hosted by the most prominent media figure in the sport. If the nose wasn’t a clear target before, it is now. Yan will make a point of peppering Dvalishvili’s nose with jabs and straight punches down the middle. Dvalishvili has a superhuman mindset and work ethic, but a nose injury that gets targeted constantly can negate his will to win

If the nose wasn’t a clear target before, it is now. Yan will make a point of peppering Dvalishvili’s nose with jabs and straight punches down the middle. Dvalishvili has a superhuman mindset and work ethic, but a nose injury that gets targeted constantly can negate his will to win. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: ‘I Think It’s Ridiculous’ – WNBA Legends Candace Parker, Tina Thompson Urge Players To ‘Stop Being So Emotional’
item.description: ‘I Think It’s Ridiculous’ – WNBA Legends Candace Parker, Tina Thompson Urge Players To ‘Stop Being So Emotional’ Hall of Fame member Tina Thompson joined Candace Parker as a special guest on “Post Moves.” During her guest appearance, Thompson highlighted one of the key differences between WNBA and NBA players. According to her, WNBA players sometimes react more emotionally, and this distinction is one of the things that separate the two leagues. She then asked the league’s stars to have more control of their emotions, which would help the WNBA’s growth. Tina Thompson Thinks WNBA Players Are Too Emotional Compared to NBA Players Over the past few years, the WNBA has experienced rapid growth in several areas. Naturally, that growth has led to more attention to each individual player. That attention has also brought more critical assessment, cynicism, and scrutiny. Thompson, a four-time champion with the now-defunct Houston Comets, shared Wednesday on “Post Moves” that the way players respond to these will affect the league’s growth. She also compared it to how NBA players respond to criticism. According to her, better emotional control will be key to helping the league become a billion-dollar industry. “Billion-dollar decisions are not emotional,” she said . “So as WNBA players, commentators, fans, or whatever, we have to stop being so emotional.” She added that there is no issue with having opinions as long as it’s not “rooted in malice.” “Accept it, move on, disagree. I don’t want to hear you talking about my mom,” she continued, drawing laughter. Parker then interjected, saying that such comments attract people. However, both agreed it’s laughable, with Parker saying, “I think it’s ridiculous.” “If we want to be paid a certain way, if we want to be treated a certain way, then we have to start acting according to those statements,” Thompson then said. “If you’re going to compare one of our greats to one of their greats, those guys receive a lot of backlash and things are being said about them. They’re not emotional about it.” Thompson was one of the WNBA’s pioneers, joining the league in its inaugural season in 1997. She was drafted first overall by the Comets, and she helped lead them to glory. Alongside fellow Hall of Famers Sheryl Swoopes and Cynthia Cooper, they were crowned the league’s first-ever champions. Their run at the top of the league would not stop there. They would win three more consecutive titles, becoming the first and only team in league history to accomplish a four-peat. MORE: ‘I Don’t Know Who’s Mentally Strong Enough’ – 2-Time WNBA Champion Questions Valkyries’ Solution To Handle Angel Reese Thompson would also go on to play three seasons for the Los Angeles Sparks from 2009 to 2011. She ended her WNBA career with a two-year stint with the Seattle Storm from 2012 to 2013. She was named to nine All-Star teams and made eight All-WNBA teams over her 17-year career. In 2018, she was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball

item.title: Maxx Crosby trade could still happen for the Lions, NFL analyst says
item.description: Maxx Crosby trade could still happen for the Lions, NFL analyst says originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Anybody who knows Detroit Lions football knows that fans of this team have salivated over the idea of Maxx Crosby going to the Lions for a long time. Crosby is a Michigan native, and he has the aggressive playing style that would just fit with Detroit. It seems like a full-circle moment to have Crosby back in his home state, but it's never come to that. Not everybody is giving up on the Crosby-to-the-Lions dream, though. One NFL analyst and expert believes there's still hope that he'll somehow, someway end up in Detroit. In a piece released on Wednesday, Oct. 21, before the NFL's Week 7 slate of games , Jordan Dajani of CBS Sports names five players he'd "like to see get a change of scenery." These are players he thinks would do well if they were traded before the November deadline. Maxx Crosby trade: Going to the Detroit Lions could give the team's defense a major boost One of those players is Crosby. He has the star defensive end linked to both the Lions and Chicago Bears . It's Crosby's aggression that would really make him a good fit with Detroit. "Crosby is one of the most aggressive and well-rounded pass rushers in the NFL," Dajani notes. "Not only does he get after quarterbacks, having recorded four double-digit sack seasons, including in 2025, but he plays a high percentage of defensive snaps each year and is effective against the run as well." According to Dajani's research, no other player has notched more tackles for loss, at 135, since Crosby was drafted back in 2019 in the fourth round. He was quite a deal at the time. Detroit obviously needs to improve its defense. It's that half of the team that's holding the Lions back, with their offense on fire. Trading for Crosby would be one way to do it. More NFL news: Maxx Crosby could still land with Bears in trade deal, NFL analyst says Cardinals 'stud' projected to land with Bills, Bengals or Jaguars in blockbuster trade Chiefs' Patrick Mahomes is doing something better than anyone else in the NFL

item.title: From bad to worse! Memphis injury confirmed at Corinthians
item.description: From bad to worse! Memphis injury confirmed at Corinthians Memphis missed Corinthians' match against Vitória due to an accumulation of yellow cards. He will also be unavailable for next Saturday's (24) clash with Vasco. The Brasileirão Matchday 32 fixture will mark Seedorf's debut in charge of Timão. The No. 10 was diagnosed with swelling in the biceps femoris muscle in his right thigh on Wednesday (21). According to ge , the club's medical department does not consider the injury serious. He is expected to return to full training next week. Gabriel Paulista has also become an injury concern after being diagnosed with a strained adductor muscle in his left leg. The clash against Vasco will be a real "decider" in the battle to avoid the relegation zone, with Timão currently in 16th place on 33 points. Vasco, meanwhile, sit 15th with 35 points and a game in hand. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

item.title: Ebola: Keyamo directs airlines to bar 46 persons linked to outbreak from flying
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, Wednesday, directed aviation authorities to place 46 persons who had contact with the Ebola-infected person on a no-fly list for 21 days to prevent the possible spread of the virus. Keyamo, who also directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, to heighten Ebola response and surveillance protocols across all international airports, said he had instructed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to immediately inform all local and international airlines about the development. He disclosed this on X, formerly Twitter, after holding a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Pate. The minister stated: “This evening, I held a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate over the Ebola scourge. He shared with me a list of 44 persons with whom the affected person came in contact at the hospital when she had developed the symptoms and an additional two persons who are her domestic staff. “Whilst efforts are ongoing to isolate them for now until there is certainty they had not been infected with the virus, the aviation authorities are required to put them on a no-fly list for at least 21 days (which is the period that the symptoms are normally expected to manifest). “I have therefore directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to immediately inform all local and international airlines of this development. I have also directed FAAN to heighten Ebola response and surveillance protocols across all international airports. Measures already being implemented by FAAN include enhanced health screenings, temperature checks, travel history tracking, digital health declarations, and strict inter-agency coordination with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, following regional outbreak alerts earlier.” Vanguard News The post Ebola: Keyamo directs airlines to bar 46 persons linked to outbreak from flying appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Broda Shaggi Reveals He Was Hit by a Stray Bullet in New Documentary
item.description: Samuel Animashaun Perry (Broda Shaggi) explains the stray bullet incident behind his months-long hiatus in a new video. If you are a fan of Broda Shaggi ‘s skits, his music, or even just his lively presence on your timelines, you must have noticed that the popular entertainer and actor has been noticeably absent from social media over the past few months. Samuel Animashaun Perry has now officially returned, bringing along a deeply moving mini-documentary that breaks his silence and reveals the terrifying life-threatening ordeal behind his sudden hiatus . The multi-AMVCA winner revealed that his unexpected break was caused by a horrific incident where he was struck by a stray bullet while returning from a shoot. Recounting the frightening moment, Broda Shaggi shared,”We were done shooting and were on our way when we got stuck in a holdup. Suddenly, I heard a loud bang and everywhere went silent. I could see people talking, but I couldn’t hear anything. Then I touched my hip and saw blood. That was when it dawned on me that I had been hit by a stray bullet.” Broda Shaggi in an eccentric futuristic costume for one of his signature video skits. The incident led to an emergency hospital admission, extensive medical procedures, and an intensive period of physical rehabilitation . For a performer whose entire craft relies on boundless physical energy, comedy, and stage presence, being bedridden and unable to move presented immense physical and emotional hurdles . In the video, he candidly reflects on the overwhelming fear of losing his mobility and the uncertainty of how he would continue doing what he loves . Tracing his road from severe setback to resurgence, the documentary shows his gradual process of learning to walk again, moving from complete immobility to crutches and eventually regaining his strength . Now stepping back in front of the camera on his own terms, Broda Shaggi is turning what could have been a tragic end into a triumphant second chapter, ready to reconnect with his fans and dive back into his creative work . Watch below The post Broda Shaggi Reveals He Was Hit by a Stray Bullet in New Documentary appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Baldur’s Gate 3 Returns With New Official Sequel Series
item.description: Baldur's Gate 3 remains one of gaming's most enduring Dungeons & Dragons role-playing games of all time, thanks to its memorable characters, branching story and deep player choice, and extremely generous support from developer Larian Studios. While Larian isn't working on the next Baldur's Gate game — the studio is focusing on a different project, Divinity — the story of Baldur's Gate 3 will continue across multiple new formats.

item.title: Xbox wants you to pay 24 to 40 cents per hour to stream games you already bought
item.description: In September, when Microsoft severely limited the game-streaming buffet available to Game Pass subscribers , the company said non-subscribers would soon be able to "purchase cloud playtime hours through the Xbox Store and stream eligible games they own on supported devices." Today, Microsoft rolled out those a la carte Cloud Playtime purchases to Xbox Insiders, with prices that might be a bit galling for players who have already purchased these streamable games. The "introductory launch pricing" for Xbox's Cloud Playtime purchases is as follows: 10 hours for $4 (~$0.40/hour) 25 hours for $8 (~$0.32/hour) 50 hours for $12 (~$0.24/hour) Purchased playtime "remains available until it’s used," Microsoft writes, so you don't have to worry about your 50-hour purchase expiring before you can use it fully. Read full article Comments

item.title: Kano will vote Tinubu in 2027, Governor Yusuf assures
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf has assured President Bola Tinubu of the support of the people of Kano State in the 2027 general election. According to him, the people of Kano will vote for the President to ensure the continuation of his development projects. Yusuf stated this on Wednesday while representing president Tinubu at the commissioning of a section of the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Highway at Tamburawa in Kano State. He praised the President for projects being executed by the Federal Government, saying that the highway would ease transportation across Northern Nigeria. Governor Yusuf also revealed that many projects executed by President Tinubu had not received adequate publicity. “I have seen many projects the President has executed that have not been publicised. I could go on and on listing the projects and initiatives of this administration,” Yusuf said. He expressed confidence that the people of Kano and other parts of the country would support Tinubu in the next general election. “The people of Kano will come out en masse to vote for President Tinubu, not only in Kano but across the North-West, the South and the country at large, to ensure the continuation of his development projects,” he added. Also speaking at the event, the Minister of Works, David Umahi, said the worst of Nigeria’s economic hardship was over. He insisted that Tinubu’s reforms were beginning to yield positive results. “The reforms have started to yield dividends of democracy. Even in the darkest hour before dawn, there is hope. Let us support President Bola Tinubu,” Umahi said. He cited road projects in Kano and other parts of the North-West as evidence of the administration’s efforts. He added that the Federal Government was working to complete projects inherited from the late President Muhammadu Buhari. “There is no project started by the late President Buhari that President Bola Tinubu is not doing in the North,” he said. Umahi listed several road projects in the region, including the Kano Northern Bypass, Kano Ring Road, Kano-Kongolam road project and the Zari-Hunkuyi road project. He also said the Federal Government was working on the Sokoto-Zamfara-Zaria road. He added that some inherited projects had been redesigned to feature reinforced concrete pavement. According to Umahi, the Tinubu administration has completed close to 400 kilometres of roads in the North-West within three years, while about 4,000 kilometres of road projects are ongoing in the region. He said the Abuja–Kaduna–Zaria–Kano Highway would benefit not only the North-West but also other parts of the country. The post Kano will vote Tinubu in 2027, Governor Yusuf assures appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Enterprises keep buying software upgrades that IT thinks will make things worse
item.description: Enterprise-sized businesses spend, on average, 28 percent of their software budgets on unwanted upgrades, migrations, and licensing changes. Often, those firms' IT heads think those changes are detrimental. Those results are according to a survey of 2,018 chief information officers and senior IT decision-makers at companies with at least 10,000 employees that Origina commissioned for its report, “ The Software Tax .” About half of the respondents (1,011) are from the US, and the rest are from the United Kingdom. All respondents worked at companies with at least $1 billion in annual revenue. Keep in mind that Origina provides maintenance for various enterprise software. Its report points to independent software maintenance as a way for IT leaders to regain control over software budgets, illustrating its potential bias. A third-party research consultancy, Censuswide , conducted the survey. Read full article Comments

item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
item.description: null On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.) It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year. The mission ended abruptly 14 months ahead of its planned end date when scientists lost contact with the probe . An Indian PSLV rocket launches the Chandrayaan-1 moon mission on Oct. 21, 2008 EDT (Oct. 22 local time in India). (Image credit: ISRO) Why it mattered The Indian Space Research Organisation , or ISRO, had a lot riding on the success of Chandrayaan-1 moon mission, which marked the first-ever deep space mission by the Indian space agency. It was also the first mission to the moon for India, a country that hopes to launch its own crewed spacecraft and build a space station. Chandrayaan-1 did more than just demonstrate that India's space program was capable of launching missions to the moon; it also returned some amazing science results, like evidence of water ice on the moon . "In September 2009, scientists published results of data collected by the American M3 instrument which had detected absorption features on the polar regions of the surface of the Moon usually linked to hydroxyl- and/ or water-bearing molecules," NASA said in a mission overview . The spacecraft carried 11 instruments to study the moon, five of them built by ISRO. The rest were experiments for the European Space Agnecy and NASA. "In addition to the five Indian instruments, the spacecraft carried scientific equipment from the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Sweden, and Bulgaria," NASA said. It took until Nov. 8, 2008 for Chandrayaan-1 to enter lunar orbit, where it stayed until contact was lost in August 2009, most likely due to a power supply failure caused by overheating. "This was short of the spacecraft’s planned two-year lifetime, although ISRO noted that at least 95% of its mission objectives had been accomplished by then," NASA wrote. NASA's Mini-SAR instrument, which flew aboard India's Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft, found more than 40 small craters with water ice. The craters range in size from 1 to 9 miles (2 to 15 km) in diameter. (Image credit: NASA) India did not stop at the moon with Chandrayaan-1. In 2019, the country launched the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter, which carried the Vikram lander and Pragyan rover. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. (Image credit: NASA) India did not stop at the moon with Chandrayaan-1. In 2019, the country launched the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter, which carried the Vikram lander and Pragyan rover. The Chandrayaan-3 misson followed in 2023, which successfully landed a new Vikram lander and Pragyan rover near the moon's south pole. India plans to launch the Chandryaan-4 mission to return moon samples to Earth in 2028 . Want more space history? item.title: Pope Leo XIV needs no further lung cancer treatment, Vatican says
item.description: Pope Leo XIV, 71, will require no further treatment for lung cancer after tests confirmed the disease was localised, the Vatican said Wednesday. The pontiff underwent surgery last week to remove part of his right lung after being diagnosed with adenocarcinoma. He was discharged Saturday and will gradually resume activities.

item.title: Tesla profits drop 43% in Q3
item.description: Tesla published its third-quarter 2026 financial results this afternoon. Earlier in October, it reported its sales and deliveries for the three-month period, selling fewer cars than in the same quarter in 2025 , yet it still beat analyst projections. Now we can see how those sales translate to the bottom line. Tesla brought in $28 billion in revenue in Q3, almost the same as in 2025. Automotive revenues were $20.6 billion, a 3 percent decrease year over year. Perhaps more troubling is the decline in revenue from solar panels and storage batteries—this line of business had been growing, but for Q3 revenue fell 16 percent year over year to $2.9 billion. Services and other revenues, though, which include parts and Supercharger use, grew by a third to $4.6 billion. But the company—like the rest of us—has seen its expenses go up. Operating expenses rose by 39 percent to $4.8 billion, dropping the company’s operating margin to just 2.6 percent; in Q3 2025, Tesla’s margin was 5.8 percent. Net profit fell to $787 million, down 43 percent year over year. What’s more, capital expenditures were up by 110 percent to $4.7 billion, and free cash flow was down 62 percent to $1.5 billion. Read full article Comments

item.title: In run-up to mass protests and riots, pro-Russian accounts amplified French anger, NGO finds
item.description: Research carried out by the Alliance4Europe NGO suggests that pro-Russian networks manipulated information online in an effort to exacerbate anger in France ahead of last weekend's massive protests and subsequent unrest. After analysing more than half a million posts across various social media platforms, the group says it was able to track the campaign back to the start of September. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Omri Preiss, Managing Director at the Alliance4Europe.

item.title: Rice Rescues Arsenal In Champions League Tie Against Bayern Munich
item.description: Declan Rice scored a late equaliser to grab last season’s runners-up Arsenal a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday. Eberechi Eze opened the scoring for Arsenal after coming on for the injured Bukayo Saka but Alphonso Davies brought Bayern level after a sublime pass from Harry Kane. Kane put Bayern on track for victory when he converted a second-half penalty, but his England teammate Rice equalised with eight minutes remaining to earn Arsenal a point. The Gunners have seven points from three games in the league phase, two more than Bayern. Bayern were without in-form winger Michael Olise, Germany captain Joshua Kimmich and midfielder Jamal Musiala. Coach Vincent Kompany had been a doubt due to illness but took his place in the dugout. “We looked dangerous, we got the goal and we had a moment there where we could have killed off the game,” Kane told DAZN. “Probably a draw was a fair result overall… There’s a lot of games and we’ve got players with injuries, players missing tonight, so we take the point and move on.” Despite the absences, the England captain ensured Bayern posed a consistent threat against Arsenal’s miserly defence with another excellent performance ahead of next week’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in Kane’s hometown of London. Kane’s second-half penalty, his 16th goal in 23 matches against Arsenal, extended his scoring streak to 10 straight Champions League games. Kane is one shy of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo, who scored in 11 consecutive matches for Real Madrid. “I had an amazing season last year, I’m extremely proud of it. The Ballon d’Or would be amazing to win, but there’s nothing I can do, the voting closed a long time ago, I have to wait for the night and see what happens,” Kane said of the award. The draw was just the second time Arsenal had dropped points in 12 games in all competitions this season. “I think it was a top-notch game for both sides,” said Arsenal forward Kai Havertz. “We can be proud of our performance, especially since it’s anything but easy to hold your own here. Bayern is one of the best teams in Europe.” Early Saka blow Arsenal’s English midfielder #07 Bukayo Saka receives medical attention after sustaining an injury during the UEFA Champions League football match between FC Bayern Munich and Arsenal FC in Munich, southern Germany on October 21, 2026. (Photo by Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND / AFP) Arsenal were hit with an early blow when Saka fell to the ground eight minutes in, grabbing his thigh and immediately signalling to the bench. With 25 minutes gone, Odegaard floated a simple pass across Bayern’s defence and into the path of the onrushing Eze, who collected and stroked the ball past Manuel Neuer. Kane put Bayern on track for victory when he converted a second-half penalty, but his England teammate Rice equalised with eight minutes remaining to earn Arsenal a point. The Gunners have seven points from three games in the league phase, two more than Bayern. Bayern were without in-form winger Michael Olise, Germany captain Joshua Kimmich and midfielder Jamal Musiala. Coach Vincent Kompany had been a doubt due to illness but took his place in the dugout. “We looked dangerous, we got the goal and we had a moment there where we could have killed off the game,” Kane told DAZN. “Probably a draw was a fair result overall… There’s a lot of games and we’ve got players with injuries, players missing tonight, so we take the point and move on.” Despite the absences, the England captain ensured Bayern posed a consistent threat against Arsenal’s miserly defence with another excellent performance ahead of next week’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in Kane’s hometown of London. Kane’s second-half penalty, his 16th goal in 23 matches against Arsenal, extended his scoring streak to 10 straight Champions League games. Kane is one shy of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo, who scored in 11 consecutive matches for Real Madrid. “I had an amazing season last year, I’m extremely proud of it. The Ballon d’Or would be amazing to win, but there’s nothing I can do, the voting closed a long time ago, I have to wait for the night and see what happens,” Kane said of the award. The draw was just the second time Arsenal had dropped points in 12 games in all competitions this season. “I think it was a top-notch game for both sides,” said Arsenal forward Kai Havertz. “We can be proud of our performance, especially since it’s anything but easy to hold your own here. Bayern is one of the best teams in Europe.” Early Saka blow Arsenal’s English midfielder #07 Bukayo Saka receives medical attention after sustaining an injury during the UEFA Champions League football match between FC Bayern Munich and Arsenal FC in Munich, southern Germany on October 21, 2026. (Photo by Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND / AFP) Arsenal were hit with an early blow when Saka fell to the ground eight minutes in, grabbing his thigh and immediately signalling to the bench. Bayern’s two previous Champions League opponents were from Norway and the perennial Bundesliga winners seemed to struggle with Arsenal’s physicality as Mikel Arteta’s side pinned them back in the early stages. With 25 minutes gone, Odegaard floated a simple pass across Bayern’s defence and into the path of the onrushing Eze, who collected and stroked the ball past Manuel Neuer. Caught out by Eze’s perfectly timed run, the hosts looked even more surprised when VAR overturned the linesman’s offside call and awarded the goal. The pre-match chatter had been dominated by talk of Kane’s Ballon d’Or prospects and he showed why he is among the favourites when he set up Davies’s equaliser 10 minutes later. Kane spotted Davies on the move and threaded the ball through the midfield and around Gabriel for the Canadian winger to guide the ball into the bottom corner. With the hosts now in the ascendancy, Ezri Konsa saw yellow for taking Kane out of a Bayern counter minutes later. After the break, Neuer and David Raya took turns producing magnificent saves, with the Bayern captain tipping Bruno Guimaraes’s header onto the crossbar and the Spaniard denying Dayot Upamecano. Both sides traded surges forward but Kane would again prove crucial as Bayern took the lead. Kane’s shot from the edge of the penalty area connected with Jurrien Timber’s arm, with the referee immediately pointing to the spot before Kane stepped up and buried his kick. Bayern looked to be in control but the match turned again when late substitute Viktor Gyokeres threaded a clever pass to Rice, who slammed in an equaliser. item.title: Meta fined $25 billion in New Mexico over Cambridge Analytica scandal
item.description: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company deceived users in a case linked to the Cambridge Analytica scandal, media reported Wednesday. The ruling follows an $18 billion settlement with 48 other states over similar claims. Meta called the penalty “a tax on speech.”

item.title: Arsenal’s Declan Rice strikes late to deny Bayern Munich after Harry Kane penalty
item.description: It is as if Harry Kane cannot get enough of tormenting Arsenal. The Bayern Munich striker has plenty of form from his Tottenham days. He remains the top scorer in north London derby history with 14 goals. He made an impact yet again here and yet it was not a night when he had the final word. That honour fell to Declan Rice, the Arsenal midfielder storming into the Bayern area in the 82nd minute to guide home a low finish that Kane would have been proud to call his own. Arsenal were hunting their latest statement result. Only once had they ever won away against Bayern – the 2-0 in the Champions League last 16 second leg in 2013, although it did not prevent an away goals exit. Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player that night. When Eberechi Eze, who came on for the injured Bukayo Saka in the 10th minute, gave them the lead midway through the first half, their hopes surged. Continue reading...

item.title: Real Madrid Rout Leipzig, Continue Perfect European Start
item.description: Real Madrid claimed a third Champions League victory in as many games by thrashing RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday, with Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande among the goals for Jose Mourinho’s side. Bernardo Silva opened the scoring for Madrid from close range towards the end of a tight first half, with Arda Guler doubling the record 15-time European champions’ advantage soon after the interval. Mbappe bent home a third before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for the German side and Diomande rammed a volley into the top corner to cap Madrid’s triumph late on. Their fourth consecutive win across all competitions will boost Madrid’s morale ahead of Sunday’s La Liga Clasico against bitter rivals Barcelona. Without a major trophy for two seasons and having endured a shaky domestic start, Madrid can at least boast a perfect record in Europe, unlike Barca after their defeat at Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday. Mourinho started with Vinicius, serving a four-match ban in La Liga, on the left flank and benched former Leipzig winger Diomande, despite his improving form. The coach also brought Bernardo Silva and Eduardo Camavinga into midfield and put midfielder Federico Valverde at right-back again, as he did in Sunday’s win at Sevilla. Real Madrid’s Ivorian forward #25 Yan Diomande (R) celebrates scoring his team’s fourth goal with Real Madrid’s French forward #10 Kylian Mbappe during their UEFA Champions League first round day 3 football match between Real Madrid CF and RB Leipzig at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium in Madrid on October 21, 2026. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP) Visitors Leipzig created the first big chance, with Madrid stopper Thibaut Courtois getting down low to make a superb save from Romulo Cardoso. Vinicius, who improved on a poor showing at Roma last week without breaking out of his rut, drew a save at full stretch from Leipzig’s Maarten Vandevoordt. Madrid carved out an advantage in the final stages of a low-key first half when Valverde cut the ball back for Guler, whose shot was saved by Vandevoordt. However the goalkeeper could not clear the ball and Silva darted in to prod over the line. It was the former Manchester City midfielder’s first goal for the club after joining this summer. Vandevoordt saved well from Valverde’s fierce effort before Guler put Madrid two goals ahead in the 52nd minute. Jude Bellingham crossed to the back post and Mbappe nodded the ball across goal, with Guler able to hold off a defender and turn home. Mbappe lashed a shot into the side-netting after being teed up by Bellingham as Madrid looked to put the game out of sight. Mourinho sent on Diomande for Vinicius with 20 minutes remaining, with the Brazilian left looking disappointed on the bench, aware he can not play again until November 4, when Madrid visit AEK Athens. Madrid’s record 140 million euro ($157m) signing Diomande pulled the ball back to Mbappe on the edge of the box for Madrid’s third, with the French forward bending home. item.title: Barkley and Buendía on target as Aston Villa maintain perfect start against Viking
item.description: For a little over half an hour, Aston Villa could look down on the rest of Europe. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed themselves another glimpse back to the days when their supremacy was undisputed. “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” the pre-match tifo display had read. Perhaps Villa really will rekindle the spirit of 1982 but the frustration here, albeit minor in the wider scheme, was that they could not maintain their birds-eye view over the continent. A superbly-taken volley by Peter Christiansen, awarded by the video assistant referee after initially being disallowed for offside, gave Viking a consolation their second-half display deserved and meant Unai Emery’s side must make do with slumming it just behind Paris Saint-Germain. Continue reading...

item.title: Real Madrid thrash Leipzig 4-1 to continue perfect European start
item.description: Real Madrid claimed a third Champions League victory in as many games by thrashing RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday, with Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande among the goals for Jose Mourinho’s side. Bernardo Silva opened the scoring for Madrid from close range towards the end of a tight first half, with Arda Guler doubling the record 15-time European champions’ advantage soon after the interval. Mbappe bent home a third before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for the German side and Diomande rammed a volley into the top corner to cap Madrid’s triumph late on. Their fourth consecutive win across all competitions will boost Madrid’s morale ahead of Sunday’s La Liga Clasico against bitter rivals Barcelona. Without a major trophy for two seasons and having endured a shaky domestic start, Madrid can at least boast a perfect record in Europe, unlike Barca after their defeat at Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday. Mourinho started with Vinicius, serving a four-match ban in La Liga, on the left flank and benched former Leipzig winger Diomande, despite his improving form. The coach also brought Bernardo Silva and Eduardo Camavinga into midfield and put midfielder Federico Valverde at right-back again, as he did in Sunday’s win at Sevilla. Visitors Leipzig created the first big chance, with Madrid stopper Thibaut Courtois getting down low to make a superb save from Romulo Cardoso. Vinicius, who improved on a poor showing at Roma last week without breaking out of his rut, drew a save at full stretch from Leipzig’s Maarten Vandevoordt. Madrid carved out an advantage in the final stages of a low-key first half when Valverde cut the ball back for Guler, whose shot was saved by Vandevoordt. However the goalkeeper could not clear the ball and Silva darted in to prod over the line. It was the former Manchester City midfielder’s first goal for the club after joining this summer. Vandevoordt saved well from Valverde’s fierce effort before Guler put Madrid two goals ahead in the 52nd minute. Jude Bellingham crossed to the back post and Mbappe nodded the ball across goal, with Guler able to hold off a defender and turn home. Mbappe lashed a shot into the side-netting after being teed up by Bellingham as Madrid looked to put the game out of sight. Mourinho sent on Diomande for Vinicius with 20 minutes remaining, with the Brazilian left looking disappointed on the bench, aware he can not play again until November 4, when Madrid visit AEK Athens. Madrid’s record 140 million euro ($157m) signing Diomande pulled the ball back to Mbappe on the edge of the box for Madrid’s third, with the French forward bending home. Leipzig quickly grabbed a consolation goal at the other end as Dean Huijsen switched off, with Gomis firing past Courtois. Diomande ended proceedings with a bang as he rattled an emphatic volley from Brahim Diaz’s cross into the top corner for his third goal in his last four appearances. item.title: UCL: Rice rescues Arsenal with late equaliser in 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich
item.description: Declan Rice scored a late equaliser as last season’s runners-up Arsenal drew 2-2 away to Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday. Eberechi Eze gave Arsenal the lead in Germany, but Alphonso Davies levelled and Harry Kane netted a penalty for the hosts before Rice made it 2-2. Rice’s goal means the Gunners have seven points from three Champions League outings, while Bayern are on five points. item.title: 2027: The Strength Of APC Is In Northern Nigeria – Basiru
item.description: The National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Ajibola Basiru, has described Northern Nigeria as the ruling party’s stronghold ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that both the region’s political elite and ordinary citizens support the party. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, Basiru expressed confidence in the APC’s prospects in the North, citing the support of prominent political figures and the establishment of a campaign office known as Arewa for Asiwaju. “The strength of the APC is in the Northern part of this country and you will see it by the grace of God when election comes in 2027. On Saturday, we had the leading lights in politics, in economy, in industry gathering together to donate a campaign office they call Arewa for Asiwaju. “Even some who are in the opposition party have changed, people like the former governor of Niger State Babangida Aliyu, now all of them are coming to join and work for the APC. The truth is that today, when you see the creme de la creme of Northern Nigeria, they are with us, you see the masses of Northern Nigeria are with us,” Basiru said. ﻿ The APC National Secretary also criticised opposition parties over their response to electoral defeats, saying they should learn to accept losses as part of the democratic process. Basiru said President Bola Tinubu had emphasised the need for politicians to accept both victory and defeat, adding that the APC had experienced losses in court cases and political contests but had moved on. “One of the things that our leader President Bola Ahmed Tinubu said is that anybody that wants that savour the joy of victory in a democracy must also be able to endure the pain when he loses. But in the case of Nigeria, it appears that the opposition only wants to win, they don’t want to lose. We have had our fair share of losses both in the court and in the political contests, and we have taken it, learn our lessons and moved on,” he said. The post 2027: The Strength Of APC Is In Northern Nigeria – Basiru appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Olamide Wants Us to Party on “Burukutu” | Watch Video
item.description: Olamide releases his new single Burukutu alongside his upcoming album Time & Space. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram When the YBNL Nation boss decides to drop new music, the entire continent pauses to listen. Olamide is back in his absolute element, and the music community is buzzing following a major surprise release that has everyone talking. Building on the momentum of his previous self-titled album Olamidé released last year, the rap icon has dropped a brand-new single while officially setting the timeline for his next massive project. Olamide’s latest single is titled “ Burukutu ”. Named after the traditional, locally brewed fermented grain beverage found across various parts of Nigeria, the track leans heavily into street-level jubilation and celebratory culture, opening with the infectious chant, “Baddoo we wanna partyyyy!” Lyrically, Olamide weaves sharp street-smart Yoruba flows with rhythmic cadences, reflecting on hustle, leisure, and local vibes over high-energy production. Olamide holding a saxophone on the courtyard set of his Burukutu music video. Photo Credit: Styling The Stars With Swazzi/Instagram The accompanying music video directed by TG Omori matches the song’s intense cultural weight visually. It cuts dynamically between a monochromatic, glowing red corridor—where Olamide appears sharply tailored in a double-breasted suit, dark sunglasses, and dreadlocks—and an earthen-toned, arched outdoor courtyard filled with rhythmic background dancers in structured white outfits, pillbox hats, and pearl details, alongside striking scenes of Olamide stepping up to play the saxophone. Alongside the release of “Burukutu,” Olamide surprised fans by announcing the official title of his forthcoming studio project: Time & Space. Marking another milestone in his legendary discography, Time & Space is officially scheduled to drop on November 16, 2026, proving yet again why the icon remains at the very heartbeat of African music. Watch the video below The post Olamide Wants Us to Party on “Burukutu” | Watch Video appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: NASA Conducts RS-25 Engine Test in Support of Future Artemis Missions
item.description: 2 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) NASA conducts a hot fire of RS-25 engine No. 10001 on the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, on Oct. 21, 2026. NASA/Danny Nowlin NASA conducts a hot fire of RS-25 engine No. 10001 on the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, on Oct. 21, 2026. NASA/Danny Nowlin NASA conducts a hot fire of RS-25 engine No. 10001 on the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, on Oct. 21, 2026. NASA/Danny Nowlin NASA tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Oct. 21 on the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. Test teams fired the developmental engine for almost eight-and-a-half minutes (500 seconds), the same amount of time RS-25 engines fire during launch of NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket. During the test, operators also fired the engine up to the 111% power level, matching the thrust needed for new production engines to launch the SLS rocket and the Orion spacecraft to orbit. The main objectives of the test were to acceptance test RS-25 flight components for future Artemis missions and validate the new thermal protection system, which protects the RS-25 engine nozzle from the thermal environment surrounding SLS during launch. While this developmental engine will not be used in flight, the hot fire test provides NASA and NASA’s prime contractor L3Harris Technologies with the capability to capture critical data to improve engine performance and reliability. Four RS-25 engines produce up to 2 million pounds of combined thrust to help launch the SLS rocket for each Artemis mission. All RS-25 engines are tested and proven flightworthy at NASA Stennis prior to use. Tests are conducted by a team of operators from NASA, L3Harris, and Nova Space Solutions. Learn More About Artemis

item.title: ‘I didn’t want to die’ – Broda Shaggi recounts stray bullet ordeal
item.description: Nigerian comedian and actor Samuel Perry, popularly known as Broda Shaggi, has recounted his near-death experience after being hit by a stray bullet during a brand activation outing. The entertainer said the incident occurred on March 9, 2026, during what began as an ordinary workday, shortly after he and his team had completed a brand activation and were leaving the location. Recounting the incident in an interview shared on his YouTube page, Broda Shaggi said, “It was just a normal day, a day I will go out for any brand activation, until the devil decided to show up. We were done with the activation, we were already leaving, and all of a sudden, I heard a loud bang, it was just total silence in the car, and then I touched my hip and saw blood, that’s when it dawned on me that I have been hit by a stray bullet.” He described the experience as frightening, revealing that he lost consciousness before reaching the hospital. “It was a crazy day, I was unconscious till we got to the hospital. All that was in my mind was just to survive, I didn’t want to die,” he said. The comedian recalled how his condition worsened to the point where medical personnel had to consider transferring him to another hospital. “It got to that point where they said they had to take me to another hospital, I was sweating, holding my leg; I was seeing blood, I just wanted to hear a doctor telling me, ‘Samuel, you’ll be fine’,” he recounted. According to him, the medical team at the second hospital quickly attended to him and moved him into the emergency room, giving him some reassurance about his chances of survival. “We got to the other hospital, they were swift, put me in the emergency room. item.content:encoded: Nigerian comedian and actor Samuel Perry, popularly known as Broda Shaggi, has recounted his near-death experience after being hit by a stray bullet during a brand activation outing. The entertainer said the incident occurred on March 9, 2026, during what began as an ordinary workday, shortly after he and his team had completed a brand activation and were leaving the location. Recounting the incident in an interview shared on his YouTube page, Broda Shaggi said, “It was just a normal day, a day I will go out for any brand activation, until the devil decided to show up. We were done with the activation, we were already leaving, and all of a sudden, I heard a loud bang, it was just total silence in the car, and then I touched my hip and saw blood, that’s when it dawned on me that I have been hit by a stray bullet.” He described the experience as frightening, revealing that he lost consciousness before reaching the hospital. “It was a crazy day, I was unconscious till we got to the hospital. All that was in my mind was just to survive, I didn’t want to die,” he said. The comedian recalled how his condition worsened to the point where medical personnel had to consider transferring him to another hospital. “It got to that point where they said they had to take me to another hospital, I was sweating, holding my leg; I was seeing blood, I just wanted to hear a doctor telling me, ‘Samuel, you’ll be fine’,” he recounted. According to him, the medical team at the second hospital quickly attended to him and moved him into the emergency room, giving him some reassurance about his chances of survival. “We got to the other hospital, they were swift, put me in the emergency room. By that time, my mind was settled and that I was going to make it through this moment,” he said. However, the reality of the incident became clearer when he realised he could no longer move his leg. “Minutes later, everything was calmed, but then I could not move my leg, that was when it dawned on me that what happened could change everything,” he said. The injury also raised concerns about his ability to continue performing the physical routines associated with his comedy character. “I was worried how do I do ‘Oya hit me’ without my leg’,” he added. Broda Shaggi said that although the pain had reduced by the following morning, he began to grapple with the emotional impact of the incident. “When I woke up the next day, the pain had reduced, but emotions started kicking in, I started asking myself ‘Why me?’” He said he eventually tried to find meaning in the experience, reflecting on his demanding work schedule and the limited time he had taken to rest since 2018. “Then I started thinking this was intentional for me to rest, because since 2018 I never rest. So I consoled myself with that.” Following the incident, Broda Shaggi travelled to Dubai for surgery. After the procedure, the comedian regained the ability to walk and stand on his two feet, marking a significant step in his recovery from the gunshot injury. Speaking about his recovery, the entertainer said he remained grateful that the incident had not resulted in worse consequences, although he had yet to recover fully. “Throughout this period, one thing I keep saying is that I am grateful because it could have been worse. It is a new reality, and I have not fully recovered yet. I am still using my crutches for now. There was a time when I could not move or even put both feet on the ground without the crutches. But now, I can walk and stand on my own without them, although I still need to use the crutches for support.” Vanguard News The post ‘I didn’t want to die’ – Broda Shaggi recounts stray bullet ordeal appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: OpenClaw creator says he spent $10 million in tokens last month
item.description: Peter Steinberger, member of technical staff at OpenAI and the creator of OpenClaw, estimates that he spent around $10 million in tokens running AI workloads last month. But don't feel bad for him, because it's all coming out of investors' pockets. He made this admission at the Cloudflare Connect 2026 conference in San Francisco on Wednesday, in a conversation with Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht. Knecht previously observed that Steinberger has acknowledged having "a virtually unlimited token budget, which not all of us in the room have." Responding to the audible surprise rising from the audience, Steinberger added, "What people don't always understand is not all of that is useful." That only amplified the murmuring, perhaps not the effect he had been after. Meanwhile, his employer, OpenAI, is reportedly trying to " accelerate funding " ahead of rival Anthropic's expected IPO. Steinberger's subsequent musing about his preferred way of working failed to recognize Knecht's acknowledgement of financial limitations. "I feel like the main challenge a lot of people still have is that our infrastructure structure hasn't really caught up yet," Steinberger said. "Like why is this still using my computer? Shouldn't this all be in the cloud?" Apart from the privacy and compliance implications of relying on cloud-based AI, cost remains a consideration for anyone not setting venture funds alight. Cloud-hosted agents can be expensive. Shouldn't this all run locally? Pointing to the OpenClaw project and how a lot of open source maintainers have given up accepting pull requests due to frustration with AI slop, Knecht asked Steinberger whether we're approaching the death of open source or a golden age of AI. Steinberger said he thinks the way pull requests are handled needs to change because people don't explain how they arrived at their proposed changed code. "If I see your thoughts, how you got from A to B, my trust in the output is way higher than if you just throw the finished work across the fence," he said. Knecht also asked Steinberger whether everyone in the room would have hundreds of AI agents running in a few years. Steinberger doubts it will be hundreds. "I think everyone will have some sort of intelligence that runs and thinks and helps them throughout the day or even predicts what could help you in the future," he said. "So instead of asking the question, maybe you already get the answer." Toward the end of the session, Knecht raised the issue of trust and how to know what data to give to an agent. That's a hard question, Steinberger admitted. Part of it, he said, has to do with how much you trust the underlying model itself, because so much of model behavior is not governed by the harness – the code that wraps the model. "A lot of decisions that I built into OpenClaw early on now can change because the models are so much better," he said. Even if risks like prompt injection have been reduced through engineering efforts, Steinberger said, "you might not

item.content:encoded: Peter Steinberger, member of technical staff at OpenAI and the creator of OpenClaw, estimates that he spent around $10 million in tokens running AI workloads last month. But don't feel bad for him, because it's all coming out of investors' pockets. He made this admission at the Cloudflare Connect 2026 conference in San Francisco on Wednesday, in a conversation with Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht. Knecht previously observed that Steinberger has acknowledged having "a virtually unlimited token budget, which not all of us in the room have." Responding to the audible surprise rising from the audience, Steinberger added, "What people don't always understand is not all of that is useful." That only amplified the murmuring, perhaps not the effect he had been after. Meanwhile, his employer, OpenAI, is reportedly trying to " accelerate funding " ahead of rival Anthropic's expected IPO. Steinberger's subsequent musing about his preferred way of working failed to recognize Knecht's acknowledgement of financial limitations. "I feel like the main challenge a lot of people still have is that our infrastructure structure hasn't really caught up yet," Steinberger said. "Like why is this still using my computer? Shouldn't this all be in the cloud?" Apart from the privacy and compliance implications of relying on cloud-based AI, cost remains a consideration for anyone not setting venture funds alight. Cloud-hosted agents can be expensive. Shouldn't this all run locally? Pointing to the OpenClaw project and how a lot of open source maintainers have given up accepting pull requests due to frustration with AI slop, Knecht asked Steinberger whether we're approaching the death of open source or a golden age of AI. Steinberger said he thinks the way pull requests are handled needs to change because people don't explain how they arrived at their proposed changed code. "If I see your thoughts, how you got from A to B, my trust in the output is way higher than if you just throw the finished work across the fence," he said. Knecht also asked Steinberger whether everyone in the room would have hundreds of AI agents running in a few years. Steinberger doubts it will be hundreds. "I think everyone will have some sort of intelligence that runs and thinks and helps them throughout the day or even predicts what could help you in the future," he said. "So instead of asking the question, maybe you already get the answer." Toward the end of the session, Knecht raised the issue of trust and how to know what data to give to an agent. That's a hard question, Steinberger admitted. Part of it, he said, has to do with how much you trust the underlying model itself, because so much of model behavior is not governed by the harness – the code that wraps the model. "A lot of decisions that I built into OpenClaw early on now can change because the models are so much better," he said. Even if risks like prompt injection have been reduced through engineering efforts, Steinberger said, "you might not want to give your agent all the permissions." Instead, he suggested using an agent to authorize your agent. "You want to have another agent that can give it permissions or not and then this agent has to negotiate with another agent," he said. "Many times the agents are like, 'oh yeah, actually maybe I shouldn't do this,' or 'there's a simpler way that keeps it within the guardrails.' So those those two systems combined greatly increase my trust that I just can let the agent rip." ®

item.title: Flying Roadsters can’t lift Tesla’s flat Q3 revenues
item.description: As the smoke clears from its outrageous Roadster demo , Tesla reported Q3 earnings on Wednesday - and the cold reality is that revenue has flatlined. Tesla said it earned $1.7 billion in net income on $28.0 billion in revenue in the quarter that ended in September 2026. Revenues were flat, while profits dropped 4 percent compared to the third quarter of 2025 , when the company earned $1.4 billion in net income on $28.1 billion in revenue. Tesla's revenue came in above Wall Street expectations of $27.9 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG . Tesla's own company-compiled expectations predicted Q3 revenues of $28.3 billion. item.title: US embassy staff, families ordered to leave Saudi Arabia
item.description: Washington has ordered non-essential US embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, the State Department said on Wednesday, as the kingdom comes under sustained deadly attacks by Yemen’s Houthis. It came after a diplomatic source told AFP that “all American staff and their families have been ordered to depart from the US embassy” in the Gulf kingdom. The source added that families of embassy staff had also been ordered to leave the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain, all of which have been targeted by Iran during the Middle East war. US State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott subsequently confirmed the order in a post on X, but said it applied to “non-emergency US government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only”. He linked the move to Houthi attacks on the country, including airports, saying “the safety and security of Department personnel and their families remain our highest priority”. Saudi Arabia has this month come under near-daily attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the kingdom’s deadliest in years, as the war with the group escalates. On Wednesday, the Saudi energy ministry said that falling debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility killed two people and injured a further two. “The attempted attack resulted in the deaths of two individuals, a Filipino and a Nepali, and injuries to two others,” the ministry said in a statement. It did not say who launched the drone aimed at Shaybah oil field near the UAE border. Earlier on Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen reported intercepting six drones. In June, a four-year-old truce in Yemen’s civil war collapsed, reviving the conflict that dates back to 2014. The Saudi-led coalition has backed the internationally recognised government since 2015. – Iran explosions – The US previously ordered non-essential staff to leave the Gulf ahead of the start of its war against Iran and again in July before US President Donald Trump called off a new wave of strikes. Late on Wednesday, Iranian state media reported the sound of explosions in the southern Hormozgan province overlooking the Strait of Hormuz, breaking a spell of relative calm. “A few minutes ago, the sound of several explosions was heard in the Karpan area of Sirik, in Hormozgan Province,” the official IRNA news agency said. It added that “local sources have not yet disclosed the nature of these explosions”. The conflict began in late February, when the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran, killing the country’s supreme leader, along with senior military commanders. Iran has attempted to blockade the strategic waterway, demanding all ships seek its authorisation to cross. In peacetime, the Hormuz strait carried around a fifth of the world’s oil supplies. item.title: UCL: Why we lost 4-1 to Como – Man United’s captain Bruno Fernandes
item.description: Man United captain Bruno Fernandes said his side lacked belief as their woes continued with a humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como on Wednesday. Man United fell behind to a second-minute goal and never recovered as the club’s winless run reached seven games after another lacklustre performance. “We started on the wrong foot, and they scored very early,” Fernandes told TNT Sports. “Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way.” The Portugal midfielder suggested Nico Paz’s early strike for Como had a damaging effect on the visitors, leaving them struggling to impose themselves. Paz scored again after Tasos Douvikas had doubled the lead, with Jacobo Ramon adding a fourth. Only a stoppage-time goal from Joshua Zirkzee stopped United from succumbing to their joint-heaviest Champions League loss. “Conceding early makes us go into the game with a mood of defeat,” said Fernandes. “It’s difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. “If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation.” Fernandes also highlighted United’s passive approach out of possession, saying Como were allowed too much time and space to dictate play. Asked whether those comments amounted to criticism of Carrick’s tactics, Fernandes declined to point the finger at his manager. “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me,” he said. “Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable. The post UCL: Why we lost 4-1 to Como – Man United’s captain Bruno Fernandes appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Reach new heights of laziness by burning tokens to let an AI tap your smartphone screen for you
item.description: Why use your smartphone when AI can do it for you? We’ve reached a new level of AI inanity with the launch of Opposable , a tool that taps, swipes, and types on Android phones and controls iPhones through a companion computer, sparing users the apparent burden of operating their own devices. If you don't want to update a calendar event, start a timer, or enable dark mode, you can apparently use an AI agent app on your computer (any client that supports MCP will do) to have Opposable do the thing for you on a connected phone. You could just do it on your computer, of course, but that’d require actually using your hands - like it’s some sort of baby’s toy . Lame. Opposable describes the purpose of its app as being to “give your AI thumbs” that allow an agent to open apps, read the screen, tap, and type, all while signed in to a device as the person too lazy to use a super-convenient technology themselves. As described in a blog post published by its creators Wednesday, Opposable's developers explain that its Android implementation uses accessibility services to inspect the screen, while screenshots provide visual input for an AI model. The model then decodes the images and figures out where it needs to tap on the screen in order to do whatever its user asked of it. The visual processing is handled by a vision-language model known as GUI-Owl 1.5 2B, running through llama.cpp, while tasks can be handled by either a paired desktop AI agent or an on-device agent that works without a desktop connection (the latter is available only on Android devices – iPhones require a companion computer, with a Mac beta available and a hardware-assisted Windows/Linux option also advertised). Even then, AI isn’t used for everything, with around 40 common tasks (setting an alarm, sending a text, switching Wi-Fi on or off) running as fixed code without an AI model involved. Opposable doesn’t appear to be particularly fast, however, and its accuracy is questionable too. Opposable’s website includes three different examples of tasks executed using its product, and none seem to merit using an AI over, you know, human hands. In one example, Claude Code over MCP is used to change the system’s theme to dark mode and then set a five-minute timer. This takes 50 seconds and requires 17 tool calls. In a second example using Claude Code and MCP, Opposable is asked to look up when Apollo 11 launched and who was on board, which takes just shy of 2 minutes. The number of tool calls isn’t mentioned, but the run cost is $0.44, which seems ridiculous when you can use your hands and figure it out for free. Hell, just asking Gemini or Siri right on a smartphone would return the answer faster and cheaper. Those half-a-buck requests to Opposable could add up pretty quickly if you’re lazy enough to justify its use. A third example shows a virtual Android device operating without a paired desktop agent, instead relying on the on-device agent that Opposable installs on Android phones. Opening t
item.dc:creator: Brandon Vigliarolo
item.content:encoded: Why use your smartphone when AI can do it for you? We’ve reached a new level of AI inanity with the launch of Opposable , a tool that taps, swipes, and types on Android phones and controls iPhones through a companion computer, sparing users the apparent burden of operating their own devices. If you don't want to update a calendar event, start a timer, or enable dark mode, you can apparently use an AI agent app on your computer (any client that supports MCP will do) to have Opposable do the thing for you on a connected phone. You could just do it on your computer, of course, but that’d require actually using your hands - like it’s some sort of baby’s toy . Lame. Opposable describes the purpose of its app as being to “give your AI thumbs” that allow an agent to open apps, read the screen, tap, and type, all while signed in to a device as the person too lazy to use a super-convenient technology themselves. As described in a blog post published by its creators Wednesday, Opposable's developers explain that its Android implementation uses accessibility services to inspect the screen, while screenshots provide visual input for an AI model. The model then decodes the images and figures out where it needs to tap on the screen in order to do whatever its user asked of it. The visual processing is handled by a vision-language model known as GUI-Owl 1.5 2B, running through llama.cpp, while tasks can be handled by either a paired desktop AI agent or an on-device agent that works without a desktop connection (the latter is available only on Android devices – iPhones require a companion computer, with a Mac beta available and a hardware-assisted Windows/Linux option also advertised). Even then, AI isn’t used for everything, with around 40 common tasks (setting an alarm, sending a text, switching Wi-Fi on or off) running as fixed code without an AI model involved. Opposable doesn’t appear to be particularly fast, however, and its accuracy is questionable too. Opposable’s website includes three different examples of tasks executed using its product, and none seem to merit using an AI over, you know, human hands. In one example, Claude Code over MCP is used to change the system’s theme to dark mode and then set a five-minute timer. This takes 50 seconds and requires 17 tool calls. In a second example using Claude Code and MCP, Opposable is asked to look up when Apollo 11 launched and who was on board, which takes just shy of 2 minutes. The number of tool calls isn’t mentioned, but the run cost is $0.44, which seems ridiculous when you can use your hands and figure it out for free. Hell, just asking Gemini or Siri right on a smartphone would return the answer faster and cheaper. Those half-a-buck requests to Opposable could add up pretty quickly if you’re lazy enough to justify its use. A third example shows a virtual Android device operating without a paired desktop agent, instead relying on the on-device agent that Opposable installs on Android phones. Opening the clock app and switching to the stopwatch tab takes it about 96 seconds, which is supposed to be impressive, apparently, as the company behind Opposable decided to showcase it on the thing’s website. As for Opposable’s ability to actually accomplish tasks, well, that’s not exactly a sure thing. “On eight tasks the model had never been tuned on, run on the emulator twice each, giving it the whole task succeeded 4 and 3 times,” the blog post notes. I’m pretty sure my brain and hands can do better without burning tokens to fail. “Giving it one subgoal at a time and checking each claimed success against the accessibility tree before the next subgoal succeeded 6 times in both rounds,” the blog continues - so even when it gets babysat each step of the way, it still only succeeds at three-quarters of tasks. Cool - that’s really going to free up all that time wasted setting timers and doing other mundane tasks on my handset. Why someone would install this on their Android device - which requires sideloading an APK and manually granting access to read and interact with the screen through accessibility settings - seems like a bit of a mystery. Opposable’s website even warns that it could be a security disaster: “whoever holds the token can operate the phone, so treat it like a password,” but still invites users to try. An argument could be made for using Opposable as an accessibility tool for people with difficulty using a smartphone, but this isn’t mentioned anywhere on its website. Opposable is instead billed as a way to “hand off the phone chores,” leaving users free to do something else - just not on the phone currently being slowly controlled by a clumsy AI. Sure, you could give your AI some virtual thumbs through Opposable, but … why? We reached out to the Opposable team to get an answer to that question, but didn’t hear back. ®
